signal_month_attribution.method: entry-notional-weighted trade return less same-window SPY return

trades.thesis: AllianceBernstein Holding L.P. is a leveraged-free but fundamentally deteriorating pass-through vehicle: its entire value derives from a ~37.5% stake in AllianceBernstein, whose qualifying revenues are explicitly disclosed as decreasing YoY, whose cash distributions to Holding fell $18.9M YoY, and whose adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted EPS declined ($0.30 vs $0.36 Q3; $1.06 vs $1.20 9M). The +80% GAAP equity-earnings surge is a base effect from lapping an $89.6M real estate charge plus ownership creep from comp-driven buybacks — not revenue momentum. Management itself flags that 'challenges are likely to continue for the remainder of 2011' including continued significant net redemptions, and warns of potential goodwill impairment if depressed valuations persist. At -42% from its 1-year high the units screen cheap, but cheapness requires a rerating mechanism to matter: none exists here. The buybacks (~7.7M units YTD) fund deferred compensation rather than representing opportunistic capital return, AXA's 60.9% control leaves minority unitholders passive, the PTP tax status is fragile, and there is an Interim CFO. In late 2011, active managers facing equity outflows had no visible inflection; the stock is a falling knife with a yield attached.
trades.catalyst: None credible within 90 days. The only dated event is the $0.26/unit distribution payable Nov 23, 2011 — a routine pass-through payout, not a rerating trigger. Unit repurchases (~$45M in Q3) are comp-funding mechanics rather than a discretionary capital-return program, and the 10b5-1 plan expires Oct 26, 2011 with no stated successor.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would be invalidated by evidence of AllianceBernstein returning to positive net flows / rising qualifying revenues (visible only via Exhibit 99.1 AUM data not supplied here), a resumption of open-market unit repurchases at materially discounted prices, or a market-wide risk-on rotation that compresses the discount of closed-end-style vehicles regardless of fundamentals.

evidence_refs.why: Adjusted diluted EPS fell to $0.30 from $0.36 (Q3) and $1.06 from $1.20 (9M) — the cleanest read on underlying per-unit economics shows deterioration, not improvement.

Filing explicitly attributes earnings growth to lapping a $89.6M Q3 2010 real estate charge while qualifying revenues decreased — headline +80% GAAP growth is a base effect, invalidating the apparent momentum signal.
Distributions received from AB fell $18.9M YoY to $145.1M and operating cash flow declined to $120.7M — the cash engine that drives the unit price is shrinking.
Management warns that prolonged depressed unit prices/net redemptions could force a goodwill impairment at AB — a discrete negative catalyst that would hit the pass-through directly.
$0.26/unit distribution declared Oct 26, 2011 confirms the full-payout structure remains intact — the one genuinely supportive fact, but it supports income, not price appreciation.

trades.thesis: The 10-Q shows a genuine Q3 inflection — revenue +32% YoY to $67.5M, gross margin ~54%, operating income +76% YoY — against a stock already down 53% from its 1-year high, so the market is pricing the weak nine-month trajectory (revenue -5%, operating income -63%, operating cash flow -$6.4M) rather than the recovering run-rate. The rerating mechanism is concrete: an $80.0M deferred revenue balance built for conversion over coming quarters, plus the company's own flagged backlog-conversion pipeline, gives a dated path for Q4 revenue recognition within the forecast window. Downside is tolerable rather than benign: covenant headroom is wide (funded debt/EBITDA 0.55:1 vs 2:1 max; $39.4M excess availability vs $5.0M minimum) and ~$54.8M of the $110M secured facility is undrawn, so the cash burn is a grind, not a solvency event, over 90 days. The setup is a momentum-inflection long at a deeply depressed price, not a cheapness-only thesis — but conviction is capped by accrual-heavy earnings ($23.7M of the working-capital drag was variable stock-comp payments), rising secured debt, and an unresolved legal/credibility overhang (prior restatement litigation, securities class actions, adverse $2.1M arbitration award under appeal).
trades.catalyst: Q4 2011 holiday-season theater system deployments converting the $80.0M deferred revenue balance into recognized revenue, with continued Q3-style momentum (equipment +36%, rentals +53% YoY) driving upward estimate revisions; secondary positive from potential collection on the $11.3M E-City ICC award.
trades.invalidation: Q4 results or interim disclosures showing theater backlog failing to convert to revenue (explicitly flagged risk), continued negative operating cash flow with further revolver draws toward covenant limits, or an adverse development in the securities class actions / Robots arbitration appeal.

evidence_refs.why: Q3 operating income $14.4M vs $8.2M (+76% YoY) with gross margin expanding to ~54% — a credible near-term earnings inflection that can drive rerating off a -53% drawdown.
Deferred revenue of $80.0M (up from $73.8M) provides a grounded, near-term revenue conversion pipeline within the 90-day window, supporting the rerating mechanism.
Funded debt/EBITDA of 0.55:1 vs 2:1 covenant and $39.4M excess availability vs $5.0M minimum makes the cash-burn scenario a slow grind rather than a near-term solvency event — tolerable downside.
Nine-month operating cash flow of -$6.4M vs +$53.7M and $39.6M drawn on a fully secured facility cap conviction and size; earnings are accrual-heavy.
Prior restatement history, securities class actions, and the adverse $2.1M arbitration award create a credibility/legal overhang that argues for a watch-tilt rather than high conviction.

trades.thesis: Mosaic trades ~41% below its 1-year high ($39.37) despite filings showing accelerating fundamentals: Q2 FY12 net sales +12.7% YoY ($3,014.5M), six-month sales +25.4%, six-month gross margin expanding to 28.4% from 26.2%, and operating earnings up 42.9% to $1,526.6M. Headline EPS decline is optical — it laps a $685.6M one-time investment-sale gain. Two credible rerating mechanisms exist beyond cheapness: (1) completion of the Cargill split-off unwind — all 112,991,398 Class B shares converted post-quarter-end, eliminating the dominant ownership overhang and normalizing float/index treatment; (2) the Dec 7, 2011 tolling agreement settlement freeing Esterhazy potash volumes for market-priced sales, which management flags as potentially materially positive. Balance sheet is a downside buffer: $3.6B cash vs ~$1.55B debt, $1.07B six-month OCF, $729M undrawn revolver, and refinancing at lower coupons. Key risks are idiosyncratic and bounded: the South Fort Meade injunction raises phosphate costs via purchased rock (mitigated by an appeal pending at the Eleventh Circuit), rising unrecognized tax benefits ($416.6M) amid IRS/CRA audits, and commodity/FX sensitivity (AOCI -$310M translation loss). As a fertilizer cyclical at a deep drawdown with strong operating momentum and dated structural catalysts, risk/reward skews favorable but with wide dispersion typical of the sector.
trades.catalyst: Completion of the Cargill split-off unwind (all 112.99M Class B shares converted to Class A post-quarter-end) removing the dominant ownership overhang, combined with the Dec 7, 2011 PCS tolling agreement settlement that frees Esterhazy potash volumes for market sales from 2012, plus upcoming Q3 FY12 earnings (March 2012) showcasing underlying operating earnings growth ex-prior-year one-time gain.
trades.invalidation: Adverse Eleventh Circuit ruling extending the South Fort Meade mining injunction into peak production periods (forcing sustained purchased-rock substitution and potential concentrate plant closures), or a sharp break in potash/phosphate pricing that reverses the gross-margin expansion trend by the Q3 FY12 report.

evidence_refs.why: Sales +12.7% YoY (six months +25.4%) with gross margin expansion and operating earnings +43% demonstrate genuine fundamental momentum behind the depressed share price.

Stockholder-approved one-for-one conversion of all 112.99M Class B shares, executed after quarter-end, completes the Cargill exit structure — a dated, concrete structural catalyst for rerating rather than mere cheapness.

Dec 7, 2011 settlement of the PCS tolling dispute frees potash volumes previously committed under the tolling agreement, with management explicitly flagging material positive effect on results — a near-term earnings lever within the forecast window.
$3.6B cash vs ~$1.55B total debt provides balance-sheet cushion that bounds downside and funds buybacks/dividends while the thesis plays out.

Second Preliminary Injunction halted Hardee County Extension mining, forcing purchased rock and threatening 3-4M tonnes of annual finished phosphate capacity if prolonged — the principal idiosyncratic downside risk.

trades.thesis: St. Joe (JOE, ~$15.24 pre-cutoff, -42% from 1y high, ~$1.4B market cap on 92.2M shares) presents an asset-value story that fails the two-part test for a long candidate. The bull case is real but slow-burning: a Jan 25, 2012 strategy pivot cutting future capex ~$190M, $15-18M annualized restructuring savings, a fortress balance sheet ($162.4M cash vs $53.5M debt), a $55.9M timber deed, first VentureCrossings tenant (ITT build-to-suit, rent starting early 2013), airport traffic up 178% since 2009, and dismissal with prejudice of the Meyer securities class action. But the rerating mechanisms are either already public (strategy shift, cost cuts, class-action dismissal were known before/at the cutoff and likely partially priced) or fall outside the 90-day window (rent commencement early 2013, bulk-sale execution unquantified). Meanwhile the dominant near-term overhang is unresolved and severe: an SEC order of private investigation covering antifraud, internal controls, books-and-records and auditor communications since 2007 — expressly implicating the same impairment practices behind the $374.8M charge and extending to Fairholme/Berkowitz Section 13(d) issues — plus pending derivative suits alleging identical conduct. Management itself concedes low operating cash generation and no significant near-term market recovery. With operations generating minimal cash, subjective impairment assumptions inviting further writedowns, and no dated catalyst inside 90 days, cheapness relative to legacy land basis is not actionable. Balance-sheet strength argues the tail is not catastrophic (impairment largely non-cash, net cash ~$109M), so this is a name to monitor for SEC-investigation resolution or concrete bulk-sale announcements rather than to own now.
trades.catalyst: No dated catalyst lands inside the 90-day window: ITT VentureCrossings rent commences early 2013, bulk-sale monetization under the Jan 25 strategy has no announced transactions, and BP/GCCF recoveries are unquantified. The only near-term potential positive is incremental disclosure of bulk land sales under the new strategy; the dominant near-term event risk is adverse news flow on the SEC investigation.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would flip to long-candidate if (a) the SEC investigation resolves without charges or is narrowed away from impairment practices, (b) a material bulk land sale under the new strategy is announced at prices validating carrying values, or (c) additional large tenants sign at VentureCrossings ahead of the 2013 rent commencement. It would harden toward reject on an SEC enforcement action, a second large impairment, or derivative-suit escalation against Berkowitz/Fairholme.

evidence_refs.why: Active SEC order of private investigation into impairment practices, antifraud, internal controls and auditor communications since 2007, naming officers/directors and 5% holders incl. Fairholme/Berkowitz — an unresolved regulatory overhang that caps rerating and creates headline risk within any 90-day window.

$(386.8)M operating loss in 2011 vs $(51.6)M in 2010, revenues ($145.3M) far below 2007-08 levels, and management explicitly expects no significant near-term market improvement — no fundamental earnings inflection available inside 90 days.

Jan 25, 2012 strategy pivot cuts planned capex ~$190M and enables bulk asset sales — a genuine self-help repositioning, but it was disclosed pre-cutoff and its cash benefits accrue gradually rather than serving as a discrete 90-day rerating trigger.
$162.4M cash vs $53.5M debt plus $55.9M timber deed proceeds limits solvency/dilution risk, making the downside tail tolerable even though it does not by itself justify a long.

Meyer securities class action dismissed with prejudice (Jan 12, 2012; amend denied Feb 14, 2012) removes one legal overhang, though derivative suits and the appeal window keep residual litigation tail risk alive.

Impairment testing rests on highly subjective assumptions (0-10% appreciation, holding periods to 13 years), which is precisely the subject of the SEC inquiry — recognition risk could force further writedowns that undermine NAV-based cheapness arguments.

trades.thesis: Amarin is a pre-revenue late-stage biopharma whose lead asset AMR101 has an SPA-backed NDA under FDA review for the MARINE indication with a hard PDUFA date of July 26, 2012. The 90-day window from the 2012-02-29 cutoff captures the classic pre-PDUFA re-rating period: SPA support plus already-reported favorable Phase 3 MARINE/ANCHOR results give an above-base-rate approval prior, while the January 2012 $150M 3.50% exchangeable notes (~$144.3M net) on top of $116.6M year-end cash provide roughly $260M pro forma liquidity — sufficient for at least twelve months including REDUCE-IT and launch prep, so financing risk does not force dilution before the catalyst. The stock sits ~55% below its 1-year high, suggesting much speculative froth has been cleared. Offsetting factors keep sizing modest: no revenue, $69.1M FY2011 loss with rapidly rising spend, unresolved Ester shareholder dispute, no internal audit function, single API supplier in the NDA, and an undated strategic-process overhang. The rerating mechanism is credible (dated, SPA-supported binary event with funded runway); downside is tolerable because cash covers operations past the decision date, but a complete response letter would be severe given ANCHOR is contingent on MARINE — hence a moderate expected excess rather than aggressive sizing.
trades.catalyst: Dated FDA PDUFA decision on July 26, 2012 for the SPA-backed AMR101 MARINE NDA; the 90-day window captures the pre-decision positioning period ahead of this binary event, with potential upside optionality from an undated strategic collaboration/acquisition process running in parallel.
trades.invalidation: Announcement of an FDA advisory committee meeting, a complete response letter or negative regulatory communications on MARINE, adverse developments in the Ester shareholder dispute, a large dilutive equity raise before approval, or breakdown below the post-offering trading range would invalidate the thesis; also any signal that REDUCE-IT enrollment is stalling, weakening the ANCHOR-dependent longer-term story.

evidence_refs.why: Quote-grounded PDUFA date of July 26, 2012 provides a hard, dated regulatory catalyst whose anticipation falls inside the 90-day window.
SPA agreement with FDA on the MARINE NDA materially raises the prior probability of approval versus an unstructured review, de-risking the binary event.

~$144.3M net proceeds from January 2012 exchangeable notes plus $116.6M year-end cash (~$260M pro forma) funds operations ≥12 months including REDUCE-IT and launch prep, removing near-term financing pressure before the PDUFA.
Pre-revenue with $69.1M FY2011 loss and sharply rising R&D costs means valuation rests entirely on the regulatory outcome; caps conviction and justifies tail-risk discount.
ANCHOR approval is contingent on MARINE approval plus outcomes study underway, so a MARINE CRL would impair both indications — the core mechanism behind the downside tail estimate.
Exchangeable notes convertible at ~$8.8125/ADS create a known dilution/overhang reference point that can cap upside if the stock approaches the exchange price.

trades.thesis: Vishay Intertechnology (VSH) screens as deep value — net cash and short-term investments of $533.5M (~38% of the ~$1.4B market cap at $8.89), covenant headroom (leverage 1.24x vs 3.25x max), long-dated debt, and a stock already 41% off its 1-year high. But cheapness alone is insufficient here. The operating trajectory is still deteriorating sharply YoY: revenue -22.5%, gross margin compressed ~550bp, operating income -59%, MOSFETs near breakeven, and operating cash flow collapsed to $22.6M from $97.8M on a working-capital/inventory build amid declining turnover. The sequential recovery story (book-to-bill 1.11, backlog rebuild) is management-narrative only, and margins were supported by explicitly 'temporary' fixed-cost reductions. Critically, there is no credible near-term rerating mechanism: no dated catalysts in the filing, buyback capacity ($306.8M) is discretionary and constrained by a secured credit facility, and substantially all cash is offshore with repatriation tax friction — so the balance-sheet value is not readily deployable to shareholders. Dual-class structure and cross-default provisions add friction. With semis in a demand trough and macro risk elevated in mid-2012, a beaten-down cyclical with falling cash flow and no hard catalyst has poor odds of positive excess return over 90 days despite asset support limiting catastrophic downside.
trades.catalyst: None dated within 90 days. Potential upside surprises would be a confirmed cyclical upturn in orders/backlog translating into Q2 revenue guidance beats, or an announced deployment of the $306.8M buyback capacity against a deeply discounted share price.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would be invalidated by a strong Q2 print showing YoY revenue stabilization plus sustained order momentum beyond temporary cost actions, or a board-authorized large buyback funded despite offshore-cash constraints — either could force a rerating toward asset value.

evidence_refs.why: Q1 revenue -22.5% YoY and operating income roughly halved confirm an active cyclical downturn, not a completed one.
Sequential margin improvement is explicitly attributed to temporary fixed-cost reductions, undermining durability of the recovery narrative.
OCF collapsed to $22.6M from $97.8M with inventory building into falling demand — internal funding of any buyback is constrained near term.
Substantially all of the headline net cash is offshore with repatriation tax friction, discounting its per-share value and limiting buyback usability.
Book-to-bill 1.11 and rebuilt backlog are genuine green shoots, but they are management assertions without quantified backlog disclosure and have not yet shown up in reported results.
$306.8M repurchase capacity is real but discretionary and conditioned on facility ratios/liquidity thresholds; not a committed catalyst.

trades.thesis: Diodes (DIOD, $19.51, -42% from 1y high) is a cyclical-trough long candidate, not a value trap, because the bear case is already priced and a dated, verifiable rerating mechanism exists within the 90-day window: Q2 2012 guidance of $155-164M revenue (+7-13% QoQ) and gross margin recovery to ~26% from 23%, with the Q2 print landing inside the forecast horizon. Corroborating early-cycle evidence is genuine rather than purely promotional: finished-goods inventory cut 20%, channel inventory down 3%, and +1% sequential revenue against normal Q1 seasonality. Downside is tolerable: $176.7M cash, $368M working capital, positive operating cash flow, low net leverage, no material litigation, and clean controls — the risk is cyclical earnings, not solvency. Skeptical discounts applied: management's "cycle low" claim contradicts its own acknowledgment of broad demand declines; earnings quality is flattered by $1.1M other operating income (Eris fair-value gains) and a 10% tax rate; the cash build is debt-funded ($40M term loan) rather than operational; and ~$15M remaining Chengdu JV capital plus a $15.9M pension deficit are real H2 cash calls. Cheapness alone is not the thesis — the thesis is guidance-confirmed sequential inflection at a deeply depressed base.
trades.catalyst: Q2 2012 earnings report (early August 2012) confirming guided sequential revenue growth of 7-13% and gross margin recovery to ~26%, validating the cycle-low call and triggering rerating of a stock still priced for continued deterioration.
trades.invalidation: Q2 results (reported within the window) miss the $155-164M revenue guide or gross margin lands below the 24% low end, indicating the cycle-low call was wrong and pricing/utilization pressure persists; alternatively, further sequential revenue decline or a cut in the CDHT/China investment timeline signaling cash strain.

evidence_refs.why: Concrete, dated near-term rerating mechanism: guided sequential revenue +7-13% and GM recovery to 26% +/-2%, verifiable at the Q2 print within the 90-day window.
Sequential inflection evidence beyond management assertion: finished goods cut 20%, channel inventory down 3%, +1% QoQ revenue against seasonal weakness — supports the trough thesis.
The bear case is fully in the price: GM 23% vs 36% YoY, operating income -80%, and the stock is down 42% from its 1-year high — sets a low base for excess return if guidance is met.
$176.7M cash, $368M working capital, positive OCF and ~$48M untapped foreign facilities make bankruptcy/liquidity tail risk remote over 90 days; downside is cyclical, not solvency.
Management's cycle-low claim is self-serving and contradicted by acknowledged pricing pressure, so it is discounted — but it is the stated basis for the Q2 guide and will be tested quickly.

Counterweight: the $47M cash build is financing-driven ($40M term loan draw), not operational; OCF of $13.4M barely covers capex, and JV/pension commitments (~$15M CDHT remainder, $15.9M pension deficit) will consume liquidity in H2.

trades.thesis: DHI (Dice Holdings) enters the window at $8.23, ~42% below its 1-year high, despite improving fundamentals: Q2 revenue +8% YoY, operating income +26% with ~32% margins, H1 Adjusted EBITDA $38.7M, and strong cash conversion ($34.2M H1 OCF vs $18.1M net income). The balance sheet is lightly levered ($50.8M cash + $5.7M investments vs $15M debt, no amortization until 2017), contingent consideration is fully settled, and the company is an active buyer of its own stock — 2.3M shares repurchased in Q2 at $9.74 avg, well above the current price, with $40.4M remaining under the March 2012 $65M authorization. That buyback is the most credible near-term support/rerating mechanism: management is demonstrably willing to absorb supply at prices ~18% above market. Valuation on ~5x annualized EV/EBITDA is undemanding. However, this is a modest-conviction candidate, not a high-conviction one: the -42% drawdown reflects a real fundamental drag (Finance segment revenue -15% YoY on European/UK macro weakness), H1 OCF declined YoY on a smaller deferred revenue build, interest expense tripled, and $177M of goodwill (~56% of assets) faces its annual Dice reporting-unit test on Aug 31 — inside the 90-day window. Small-cap liquidity (~$3.6M/day) limits institutional sponsorship. The setup is cheap with a self-help catalyst and tolerable downside, but no confirmed inflection; the bet is that continued buyback execution plus a clean Q3 print (late October, within window) stabilizes the multiple.
trades.catalyst: Continued open-market buybacks under the $40.4M remaining Plan II authorization (management repurchased at $9.74 avg vs. $8.23 current price), plus Q3 2012 earnings in late October within the window demonstrating sustained Tech & Clearance/Energy momentum and margin expansion; passing the Aug 31 Dice goodwill test removes a binary overhang.
trades.invalidation: Q3 2012 results (late October) showing consolidated revenue deceleration or further Finance-segment erosion; suspension or completion of buybacks without reauthorization; any goodwill impairment indication at the Aug 31 Dice test; sustained cash burn pushing the balance sheet from net cash toward net debt.

evidence_refs.why: Company repurchased ~2.3M shares at avg $9.74 in Q2 vs. $8.23 pre-cutoff price — an active, price-insensitive buyer ~18% above market with $40.4M authorization remaining; the most concrete near-term support/rerating mechanism available.

Q2 operating income +26% YoY on ~1% opex growth (32% margin) shows real operating leverage; Tech & Clearance +14% and Energy +25% offset Finance -15%, supporting a growth-multiple rerating if Q3 confirms.

$50.8M cash + $5.7M investments vs. only $15.0M debt (no amortization until 2017) gives a net-cash balance sheet and limits fundamental downside; H1 Adjusted EBITDA of $38.7M implies a modest EV/EBITDA multiple at the current price.

$177M goodwill (~56% of assets) faces its annual Dice test Aug 31 — inside the 90-day window; 2011 fair values were 'substantially in excess' of carrying value, but a European-macro-driven writedown is the key tail risk.

Finance segment revenue -15.3% YoY on European debt crisis/UK recession is the fundamental drag explaining the -42% drawdown; if Europe stabilizes this segment is the swing factor, but it caps conviction.

trades.thesis: The issuer (a Houston-based E&C firm) trades ~41% below its 1-year high at $18.78 despite a $15.2B backlog boosted by the Ichthys LNG award, a fortress balance sheet (minimal recourse debt, $824M cash), and an active buyback repurchasing above the current price. Fundamentals are genuinely weak — Q2 revenue -16% YoY, IGP segment income down 61%, H1 operating cash flow -$55M, and a surge in unapproved claims/change-order revenue ($138M vs $31M) — which explains the drawdown and argues against blind value. However, unlike a mere cheap stock, there are credible dated rerating mechanisms inside the 90-day window: (1) the PEMEX $356M arbitration award enforcement reaches a Second Circuit remand hearing in September 2012 with $395M collateral already posted — collection would equal roughly a quarter of the depressed market cap; (2) $43M of the contested change orders were already customer-approved in July 2012, partially validating the claims-driven revenue and de-risking the accounting-quality concern; (3) the electrocution suit dismissal (July 13) and pending burn pit MTD ruling remove/clarify litigation overhangs. Downside appears tolerable because the balance sheet limits distress scenarios and the buyback anchors valuation. Net: asymmetric setup where partial catalyst success offsets fundamental decay, sized conservatively given negative cash generation and government-contract audit exposure ($349M DCAA suspensions, $96M demand letters).
trades.catalyst: PEMEX Second Circuit remand briefing/hearing Aug-Sep 2012 on the ~$356M award ($395M collateral already posted); burn pit MTD ruling expected 2H 2012; continued conversion of the $138M unapproved claims pool (already $43M approved in July).
trades.invalidation: Adverse PEMEX Second Circuit ruling or further Mexican court nullification of the award; acceleration of U.S. government payment suspensions/debarment risk; another quarter of steep IGP decline with continued unbilled receivables build and no claim approvals.

evidence_refs.why: Dated, high-materiality rerating event inside the 90-day window: $356M award enforcement hearing Sept 2012 with $395M collateral posted — large relative to the issuer's depressed equity value.
$43M of the disputed change orders were approved by the customer in July 2012, partially validating the aggressive claims revenue and reducing the worst-case earnings-quality scenario.
Core bear case: IGP revenue -45% YoY and total operating income down to $129M from $169M caps conviction and justifies the discount.
-$55M H1 operating cash flow and unbilled receivables build to $710M are genuine working-capital red flags that limit position sizing despite the catalyst setup.
Active repurchase (695K shares at avg $24.29, above current price) with 7.7M shares remaining provides valuation support at the depressed level.
Minimal recourse debt and large cash position make downside tail scenarios less equity-destructive than typical E&C distress cases.

trades.thesis: Barnes Group trades ~40% below its 1-year high (~$25.14) on a fundamentally stable profile: Q2 2012 operating income up YoY ($34.1M, margin 11.3%->11.6%), H1 organic growth of $17.5M across all three segments, positive FCF (~$18M), light covenant leverage (1.81x vs 3.25x max), a $750M expanded credit facility, resumed buybacks and a raised dividend. However, the filing offers no credible near-term rerating mechanism: the $335M Synventive acquisition (closing ~Aug 2012) was announced pre-cutoff and its accretion is undisclosed, while two dated risk catalysts sit inside the 90-day window — the U.S. Tax Court decision on a ~$16.5M IRS assessment (late Q4 2012/H1 2013) that management concedes could be material to any single period, and Singapore Pioneer certificate expiries pressuring the Aerospace tax rate. Offsets include YTD gross margin compression, H1 operating cash flow down $6.7M YoY, declining Aerospace RSP aftermarket sales, and a $25.2M FX translation loss. Cheapness plus balance-sheet strength is real, but the required rerating catalyst is absent; the IRS decision is as likely a negative catalyst as a positive one.
trades.catalyst: Synventive acquisition close in August 2012 with pro-forma leverage still light (1.81x vs 3.25x covenant); secondary: BDE escrow release Aug 31, 2012. Neither is a strong rerating trigger — the deal was announced pre-cutoff and the escrow is immaterial (~$11M).
trades.invalidation: Adverse Tax Court ruling with a material damages award, disclosure that Synventive economics are dilutive or integration costs exceed plan, or renewed Aerospace RSP aftermarket decline pressuring the highest-margin revenue stream.

evidence_refs.why: Q2 operating income up to $34.1M with margin 11.3%->11.6% and H1 organic growth of $17.5M across all segments — fundamentals are stable-to-improving, not deteriorating, despite the 40% drawdown.

The only dated near-term event is the $335M Synventive close (Aug 2012); it was announced July 16 pre-cutoff, so it is largely priced in and its accretion is undisclosed — insufficient as a rerating mechanism.
Tax Court decision on ~$16.5M IRS assessment expected late Q4 2012/H1 2013, with management conceding it could be material to any one period — an unresolved binary overhang inside the 90-day window.
Senior Debt/EBITDA 1.81x vs 3.25x max, $750M expanded facility, positive H1 FCF — balance-sheet risk is tolerable, limiting downside tail severity.
H1 operating cash flow fell $6.7M YoY and YTD gross margin compressed — quality-of-earnings softness that undercuts the cheapness thesis as a standalone buy signal.

trades.thesis: Crocs screens as a statistically cheap, debt-free grower: Q2 2012 revenue +12% YoY to $330.9M, diluted EPS $0.68, gross margin ~59%, $278.8M cash against negligible borrowings (~$83K), positive H1 FCF, and Asia segment compounding at +20% with the highest margins. At $15.58 — roughly half its 1-year high — the market cap (~$1.3-1.4B) implies a single-digit earnings multiple even before netting ~$279M of cash, so expectations are depressed. However, this is cheapness without a credible near-term rerating mechanism: the only dated events inside the 90-day window are adverse-skewed binaries (Spectrum Brands UK appeal ruling pending after the July 4 hearing with unquantified damages, and a U.S. Customs audit report expected H2 2012 with loss 'not estimable' against just $0.4M accrued), no disclosed buyback/dividend program to monetize the cash, working capital building faster than sales (AR +56%, inventory +28% YTD; allowance up; OCF of $49.7M trailing net income of $89.9M), Europe revenue and operating income declining, and nearly all cash trapped offshore (~$38M repatriation tax, $35.2M potentially restricted). Fundamentals argue the stock should not be at these levels; the catalyst calendar argues it may stay there or lower for another quarter.
trades.catalyst: No confirmed positive catalyst inside 90 days; nearest dated events are risk-skewed (Spectrum UK appeal ruling already heard, U.S. Customs audit report expected H2 2012). Potential upside triggers would be an acquittal-style Spectrum ruling, initiation of shareholder capital returns against the offshore cash pile, or Q3 results confirming Asia-led momentum despite Europe weakness.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if the U.S. Customs audit produces a material duty assessment, the Spectrum appeal ruling assigns large uninsured damages, Q3 shows wholesale order cancellations/inventory correction (AR+inventory build converting to markdowns), or Asia growth decelerates below ~10% — any of which would break both the rerating mechanism and the downside-tolerance condition.

evidence_refs.why: Q2 revenue +12% YoY to $330.9M with gross margin expansion and operating income +15%; Asia segment (+20%, highest margin) provides genuine fundamental momentum supporting the value case.
$278.8M cash with essentially zero debt (~20% of market cap at $15.58) plus positive H1 FCF (~$29M) creates a hard asset floor and limits balance-sheet downside.

U.S. Customs audit report covering 2006-present due H2 2012 with unestimable loss and only $0.4M accrued — a dated binary overhang landing squarely inside the 90-day window that caps the position sizing case.
Adverse UK liability finding with appeal ruling pending and unquantified damages adds a second unresolved legal tail; company narrative contradicts court finding.

AR +56% and inventory +28% YTD outpacing sales, allowance rising, provision swinging to expense, and OCF ($49.7M) well below net income ($89.9M) flag earnings-quality/working-capital risk that discounts headline P/E.
Europe revenue and operating income (-25%) declining amid macro stress removes one growth leg and raises the odds of forward estimate cuts.

trades.thesis: Strayer is a deeply de-rated for-profit educator (-47% from 1-year high, ~$56) where the bear case is fully priced in reported results but the leading indicators are turning: Q2 2012 new student enrollments grew +12% even as continuing enrollments fell -13% and revenue dropped -11%. Management explicitly guides to continued 2012 enrollment/revenue pressure from the 19% decline in 2011 new students, so trailing fundamentals (operating income -28%, H1 OCF halved to $42.7M, unearned tuition -$12.2M) should stay ugly for another 2-3 quarters — but the market prices the inflection, not the trough. Simultaneously, the dominant sector overhang is resolving: ED's own June 21, 2012 illustrative data showed ALL Strayer programs comply with gainful employment rules, most GE regulations were vacated June 30, 2012, and the DOE appeal deadline (Aug 29, 2012) falls inside the 90-day window. Downside is cushioned by a real balance sheet ($48.7M cash, only $85M term loan post-repayment, swap-fixed ~3.6%, covenant-compliant, no goodwill impairment risk of consequence at $6.8M), a ~7% dividend yield, and $80M of unused buyback authorization. This is not cheapness alone: there is a specific, dated rerating mechanism (regulatory clearance + fall-term enrollment data confirming the new-student inflection ahead of the Q3 print). Risks are real — one quarter of new-student growth is thin evidence, cost deleveraging means EPS keeps falling, and the March 2014 maturity wall looms beyond the window — so this is a sized, catalyst-driven candidate rather than a high-conviction core holding.
trades.catalyst: DOE's August 29, 2012 notice-of-appeal decision on the vacated gainful employment rule, followed by fall-term enrollment disclosures and the Q3 print (due late October) that would confirm whether the +12% new-student inflection persists against the disclosed continuing-student drag.
trades.invalidation: Fall-term start data showing new-student growth failing to persist (reverting negative) or Q3 guidance implying accelerating revenue declines; also an adverse DOE appeal reinstating gainful-employment uncertainty, or dividend/buyback retrenchment signaling management sees deeper erosion.

evidence_refs.why: New student enrollments +12% vs continuing -13% is the first credible leading-indicator inflection after the 19% 2011 new-student collapse; if sustained into fall term, it front-runs the revenue trough and provides the rerating mechanism.

ED illustrative data shows all Strayer programs compliant with gainful employment rules (first exposure year 2015) and most rules vacated June 30, 2012 — removes the primary sector-level regulatory discount driver.
Dated near-term catalyst: DOE appeal deadline Aug 29, 2012 resolves the last regulatory overhang within the forecast window.

Counterweight: operating income -28% YoY with severe fixed-cost deleveraging (instruction ratio 46.6%→51.7%) means reported earnings likely keep falling near-term; caps conviction and position sizing.

~7% dividend yield plus $80M remaining buyback authorization against a stock already down ~47% from its 1-year high limits downside and signals management willingness to deploy capital at these levels.
$48.7M cash, $85M undrawn revolver, swap-fixed ~3.6% term-loan rate, covenant compliance, and post-quarter full revolver repayment make distress/refinancing risk remote inside 90 days.

trades.thesis: ADTRAN screens optically cheap — stock down ~45% from its 1-year high at $16.30, with a fortress balance sheet (~$555M cash + AFS investments vs only $46.5M bonds payable against $713M equity), a maintained $0.09/qtr dividend, and management buying back stock aggressively into weakness ($21.08 avg in early Q3). But the fundamental trajectory argues against a long candidate within 90 days: Q2 operating income halved YoY ($26.8M vs $51.3M) on flat revenue, gross margin compressed sharply, H1 sales fell ~9%, H1 operating cash flow dropped ~44% ($37.0M vs $65.7M) on a $43M AR build (DSO 40→59 days), inventory rose 18% against declining sales, and the newly acquired NSN BBA business is loss-making ($(0.4)M pre-tax on $22.6M revenue since May 4; $(15.5)M pro forma H1). There is no credible near-term rerating mechanism in the record — no dated positive catalysts, integration costs continuing, an expired R&D credit adding tax headwind, and a pending pension obligation verification. The balance sheet caps downside but does not create upside; a deep-value/asset-support story without an earnings inflection typically drifts with deteriorating estimates. Skeptical base rate on beaten-down hardware names with halving operating income and no catalyst favors underperformance versus SPY over 90 days.
trades.catalyst: None credible within 90 days identified in filings: no dated positive events; the only forward-looking items are continued integration losses from NSN BBA, pending pension obligation verification, and a higher tax rate absent R&D credit reinstatement. Capital returns (dividend + accelerating buybacks at $21.08 avg) provide support but not a rerating trigger.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would be invalidated by evidence of Carrier Networks order recovery/backlog inflection, rapid NSN BBA path to profitability, reversal of the AR/inventory builds restoring cash conversion, or a macro/sector catalyst (e.g., broadband stimulus, carrier capex upcycle) that re-rates the stock despite soft reported results.

evidence_refs.why: Q2 operating income halved YoY ($26.8M vs $51.3M) on flat revenue — margin compression is the core problem, not a one-off
H1 operating cash flow fell to $37.0M from $65.7M on a large AR build — deteriorating cash conversion undermines the value floor argument near term
The strategic acquisition is loss-making ($(0.4)M pre-tax on $22.6M revenue; $(15.5)M pro forma H1), so the deal dilutes rather than fixes the earnings trajectory
~$555M cash+investments vs only $46.5M debt limits downside tail risk and supports the dividend/buyback, but cheapness alone is insufficient for a long candidate
Management repurchasing at $21.08 avg post-quarter-end signals insider conviction below $21, a mild support signal — yet insufficient as a rerating mechanism

trades.thesis: Kronos Worldwide is a deep-cyclical TiO2 producer trading ~47% below its 1-year high ($6.57) after a brutal Q3 2012: net sales -14% y/y, gross margin collapsed from 38% to 18%, utilization cut to ~71% of capacity, ASPs down 7% sequentially with further Q4 declines guided, ~$25M unabsorbed fixed costs and ~$85M higher raw material costs absorbed, and nine-month operating cash flow down to $57.5M from $243.4M on a $160M inventory build. The bull case would be classic trough-cycle mean reversion on a washed-out valuation, and downside is bounded by a genuinely repaired balance sheet ($120.4M cash, $125M undrawn NA revolver, €85M/$110M European facility extended to Sept 2017, $400M term loan replacing 6.5% notes at lower rates, covenants in compliance). However, the filings disclose no dated positive catalyst, management explicitly guides Q4 operating income significantly lower, pricing is still falling, and the inventory build creates further write-down/cash-burn risk if weakness persists. Entrenched Simmons/Contran control (~80% via Valhi/NL), pervasive related-party exposure ($167.6M Valhi note, all marketable securities are related-party shares), a 'temporary' OTTIM judgment on TIMET that invites a future impairment charge, and a ~$15.9M Canadian tax dispute add idiosyncratic overhang without offsetting upside mechanisms. Cheapness here reflects genuine, still-deteriorating fundamentals; a credible near-term rerating mechanism is absent. This warrants a watch position: the setup could become attractive quickly if ASPs stabilize or the inventory build reverses, but entering now is paying for a turnaround that has not yet shown any inflection in the data.
trades.catalyst: No dated positive catalyst disclosed. Potential watch triggers: sequential stabilization of TiO2 selling prices after the 7% Q3-over-Q2 decline, evidence of customer inventory destocking reversing the $160M producer inventory build, capacity utilization recovering from ~71%, or a Q4 print that clears the guided-down bar and marks the cycle trough.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated if Q4 2012 results show continued double-digit volume declines with another sequential ASP drop and no inventory drawdown, or if covenant headroom narrows such that revolver reliance becomes structural rather than bridge — either would signal a longer, deeper trough than the 90-day window can reward.

evidence_refs.why: Q3 gross margin 18% vs 38% y/y and operating margin 8% vs 28% confirm an active, not completed, downturn — the core reason cheapness alone cannot support a long.
ASPs fell 7% sequentially with further Q4 declines guided; the price/mix leg of the cycle is still moving against the company through the forecast window's first months.

$120.4M cash plus $125M NA revolver, €85M European facility, and $100M term loan accordion, with debt maturities pushed to 2017, make forced deleveraging/dilution unlikely within 90 days — this bounds the downside tail.
9M OCF of $57.5M vs $243.4M driven by a $158M inventory build shows cash burn into a falling-price environment; if prices keep sliding, inventory write-down risk adds to the bear case.
The 'temporary' OTTIM judgment on TIMET ($19.4M below cost since Oct 2011) is a latent income-statement impairment risk that could hit sentiment even if economically minor.

~80% insider control via Valhi/NL/Contran, all marketable securities being related-party stock, and a growing $167.6M Valhi note reduce the likelihood of shareholder-friendly catalysts or takeover premium.

trades.thesis: Boyd Gaming enters the window deeply de-rated (-44% from 1-year high, ~$5.04 price, ~$1.4B equity vs ~$3.9B debt) with a single, well-defined near-term event: the ~$1.45B all-debt-financed Peninsula Gaming acquisition contractually required to close by February 2013, with financing fully secured ($350M 8.375% notes held in escrow plus committed $825M term loan). Closing folds substantial acquired EBITDA into a small equity base — a classic leveraged-equity rerating setup where the stock behaves as a call option on the deal. Critically, the downside is structurally bounded: if the deal fails, the escrowed notes face special mandatory redemption, so the equity does not absorb incremental debt from a broken deal. The bear case is real — Q3 swung to a $(15.8)M net loss as interest expense ($74.1M) exceeded operating income ($48.3M), SG&A and promotional costs grew faster than revenue, operating cash flow declined YoY, current maturities jumped to $403M, and management explicitly depends on revolver availability — but most of this distress appears priced into a stock already down 44%. The bet is that successful closing within the window converts a distressed-looking balance sheet story into a higher-EBITDA, refinancing-capable story, producing positive skew from the current depressed base. Cheapness alone would not qualify; here cheapness coincides with a dated, financed, contractual catalyst.
trades.catalyst: Peninsula Gaming acquisition closing in Q4 2012 (contractual outside date February 2013), which immediately folds acquired property cash flows into the consolidated entity against a small ~$1.4B equity base; any post-close deleveraging guidance or improved pro forma disclosure is an additional rerating trigger within the window.
trades.invalidation: Regulatory approval not obtained and the merger is terminated or pushed beyond February 2013 without a credible new timeline — the escrowed notes are then mandatorily redeemed, leaving the standalone business with declining operating cash flow, rising interest expense, margin compression, and $403M of current maturities against thin free cash flow.

evidence_refs.why: Dated, imminent catalyst inside the 90-day window: ~$1.45B acquisition expected to close Q4 2012, materially increasing consolidated EBITDA relative to the small equity base.
$350M 8.375% notes held in escrow with special mandatory redemption if the merger fails by Feb 2013 — financing certainty plus a structural floor on deal-break downside.
Full acquisition financing stack ($825M term loan, $50M revolver, $350M notes) already committed and funded into escrow, removing funding risk as an obstacle to closing.
Q3 net loss of $(15.8)M driven by interest expense exceeding operating income explains the -44% drawdown and keeps expectations low; this is the bearish counterweight that caps conviction.
Current maturities jumped to $403M from $43M and management language signals refinancing dependence — genuine tail risk if capital markets or the deal close falter.
Base business still growing (+3.9% Q3 revenue), so the equity is not melting down while it waits for the catalyst.

trades.thesis: Zumiez enters December 2012 down ~52% from its 1-year high ($20.07 close) with a fundamentally mixed but survivable setup. Bull case: top-line momentum remains solid (Q3 sales +16.9%, comps +3.7%, ecommerce mix up to 10.7% from 6.4%), the balance sheet is a fortress (~$98M cash+securities, negligible debt, undrawn $25M revolver), and the board authorized a fresh $22M buyback on Nov 13, 2012 — a concrete management signal near a 52-week-low area. Much of the margin deterioration is identifiable and partly transitory (80bps from the Blue Tomato inventory step-up charge, elevated ecommerce fulfillment investment), suggesting reported profit decline overstates underlying erosion. Bear case is real: Q3 operating profit fell YoY ($21.4M vs $22.8M) on SG&A deleverage, comp growth is ticket-driven with declining transactions/units, inventories are up ~69% YTD ahead of holiday, Blue Tomato is loss-making ($1.8M net loss on $9.6M sales) with up to $28.6M earnout drag, and the annual goodwill/intangible impairment test lands in the quarter ending Feb 2, 2013. On balance, the stock's deep drawdown prices substantial pessimism while sales momentum, net cash (~$3+/share), and the buyback cap downside; a clean holiday quarter (reported within the 90-day window) is the plausible rerating trigger. This is a modest-conviction, position-size-limited long, not a high-conviction one — margin trajectory, not revenue, decides the outcome.
trades.catalyst: Fiscal Q4/holiday results (quarter ending 2013-02-02, reported ~March 2013): if comps hold mid-single-digit positive and gross margin stabilizes as the Blue Tomato inventory step-up laps (~5-month amortization ending around year-end), the market could re-rate a stock priced for comp/margin decay; the newly authorized $22M buyback provides incremental support into that print.
trades.invalidation: Weak holiday comp trends or guidance cuts at the March 2013 report (comps turning negative, further gross-margin erosion beyond the step-up roll-off, or an impairment charge against the $61.9M goodwill / $13.6M trade names); also a markdown-driven inventory liquidation signal would invalidate the washout-rerating thesis.

evidence_refs.why: +3.7% comps and 48 net new stores show demand intact despite margin noise
Operating profit declined YoY with SG&A deleverage — the key bear fact capping position sizing
$22M repurchase authorized Nov 13, 2012 signals management conviction and provides a floor bid
Undrawn revolver plus ~$98M liquid assets make downside scenarios survivable without dilution
$61.9M goodwill post-acquisition with annual impairment test in the Feb 2, 2013 quarter is a discrete tail risk
Inventory +69% vs sales +17% risks markdowns if holiday demand disappoints

trades.thesis: Apple trades ~42% below its 1-year high after a quarter of severe margin compression (gross margin 47.4%→37.5%, operating income -18% YoY despite +11% revenue growth). The bear case on unit economics is already heavily priced in. What changes the setup is a concrete, freshly executed rerating mechanism: on 2013-04-23/24 the company disclosed a buyback authorization increase from $10B to $60B (~7% of the 938.6M share count), a 15% dividend hike to $3.05/share, and a completed $1.95B ASR at $478.20 — funded by $144.7B of cash/securities growing $23.4B in six months and $35.9B of six-month operating cash flow that exceeds net income (high earnings quality). This is not cheapness alone; it is an active per-share value accrual program announced one day before cutoff, with execution visible within the 90-day window. Offsets are real: negative operating leverage (R&D +33%), payables unwind (-$4.4B), inventory build (+57%), rising warranty true-ups ($414M prior-period), and $13.8B purchase commitments — so I size conviction modestly rather than aggressively.
trades.catalyst: Freshly announced capital-return expansion (2013-04-23/24): buyback authorization raised to $60B with an active ASR at $478.20/share, plus a 15% dividend increase — a direct per-share value and yield-support mechanism executing over the next 90 days, amplified by the stock's depressed post-drawdown positioning into the next earnings cycle.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if margin compression accelerates beyond what capital returns can offset — e.g., evidence of further gross-margin erosion below ~35%, aggressive carrier price-protection redemptions flagged in MD&A, or a slowdown/suspension of buyback execution; also invalidated if the stock re-rates down on guidance cuts rather than being supported by per-share shrinkage.

evidence_refs.why: $60B repurchase authorization (~7% of shares outstanding at ~$938.6M shares) is a concrete, near-term rerating mechanism, not just static cheapness.
Dividend raised 15% to $3.05/share announced one day before cutoff — signals board confidence and adds yield support at a depressed price.
$144.7B cash/securities (+$23.4B in six months) makes the capital-return program fully fundable; downside tail is limited by balance-sheet strength.

Gross margin fell from 47.4% to 37.5% with operating income -18% YoY — the fundamental deterioration that caps upside and explains the -42% drawdown; thesis depends on capital returns offsetting this, not on margin recovery.
R&D +33% and SG&A +14% vs +11% revenue growth shows negative operating leverage persisting near term — key risk if product momentum stays soft.
$35.9B six-month operating cash flow exceeding net income confirms earnings quality despite reported profit decline; supports sustainability of returns.
Company anticipates funding dividends/buybacks partly via borrowings due to offshore cash ($102B+) — manageable but flags repatriation friction on the capital-return story.

trades.thesis: The company enters the window having just closed the $550M BDNA divestiture (Apr 22, 2013) with ~$480M immediately applied to revolver paydown — a genuine, dated balance-sheet transformation that relieves thin covenant headroom (3.13x vs 3.25x max pre-paydown) and leaves an expanded buyback authorization (4.5M shares remaining). Operating cash flow also inflected positively ($17.7M vs $6.3M YoY). However, the rerating case is weaker than the headline numbers suggest: the +18% revenue growth is almost entirely acquired (Synventive $40.3M vs only +$1.9M organic), Aerospace margins are deteriorating on flat sales, and operating margin compressed to 9.5% on a $10.5M one-time CEO-transition stock comp charge. Near-term reported earnings face identified drags within the 90-day window itself: a possible ~$20M income tax charge in Q2 2013 and ~$13M cash assessment in Q3 2013 from the adverse Apr 16, 2013 Tax Court decision, plus a normalized higher effective tax rate (21.4%), and $55.6M of convertible notes now current ahead of a March 2014 holder put. With the stock already down ~56% from its 1-year high, substantial negativity appears priced, but the deleveraging catalyst is disclosed and likely partially reflected, and there is no evidence of positive organic momentum to drive multiple expansion. Cheapness/balance-sheet repair alone does not meet the bar for a long candidate without a demand-side inflection.
trades.catalyst: Post-close deployment of remaining BDNA proceeds into announced share repurchases (4.5M-share authorization) and/or a bolt-on acquisition, plus resolution/appeal clarity on the Tax Court matter; secondary: Q2 print demonstrating Industrial margin hold ex-one-time comp charge.
trades.invalidation: Q2 2013 results showing continued Aerospace margin erosion and negative organic growth alongside the ~$20M tax charge; failure to deploy proceeds into repurchases/M&A within two quarters; adverse developments in the Tax Court appeal window or larger-than-guided assessment; any sign the March 2014 convertible put forces dilutive or expensive refinancing.

evidence_refs.why: $550M BDNA sale closed 2013-04-22 (~$400M after-tax, ~$200M gain) — the central balance-sheet transformation event inside the forecast window
~$480M immediately applied to the revolver post-cutoff; deleveraging of this scale vs. equity base is the only concrete rerating mechanism, but it is disclosed and likely partially priced
Organic sales only +$1.9M vs. $40.3M from Synventive — headline +18% growth masks ~flat underlying demand, undermining a demand-driven re-rating case
Adverse Tax Court decision (Apr 16, 2013) with penalties creates dated earnings/cash drags (up to ~$20M charge Q2, ~$13M cash Q3) squarely inside the 90-day window
Senior Debt Ratio at 3.13x vs 3.25x max pre-paydown shows how leveraged the entity was; relief is real but confirms prior balance-sheet stress
Operating cash flow improved to $17.7M from $6.3M with inventory reduction — genuine internal cash generation supports the post-deal equity story

trades.thesis: This is F5-style ADN vendor trading at $78.70, ~40% below its 1-year high, after fiscal Q2 FY2013 showed product revenue -9.8% YoY and operating income -11.7% YoY on negative operating leverage (opex +11.3% vs revenue +3.1%). The bear case is already substantially priced in: the drawdown reflects a growth-deceleration narrative, not balance-sheet or accounting distress. Offsetting strengths are real — ~82.8% stable gross margins, $1.19B cash/investments with no debt, $225.5M six-month operating cash flow, deferred revenue growth ($396.7M current vs $352.6M) evidencing sticky maintenance backlog, and an aggressive buyback ($277.2M remaining authorization, ~4.5% of market cap, executed at avg $70.13 — below the current price). However, the filing gives no evidence yet that product demand has stabilized, and R&D/SBC cost growth ($118.6M unrecognized SBC) pressures margins for at least two more years. Cheapness relative to history is not established cheapness versus a de-rating growth profile; without a confirmed inflection, this is a well-supported value trap candidate rather than a clear long. The setup argues for watching for confirmation (product revenue stabilization, expense discipline) before entry, with the next quarterly print as the natural checkpoint.
trades.catalyst: Fiscal Q3 FY2013 earnings report (expected late July 2013, within the 90-day window): any stabilization in product revenue or reiteration of full-year targets against reset expectations could drive a sharp rerating, amplified by ongoing open-market repurchases under the fresh $200M authorization.
trades.invalidation: Next quarterly results showing further product revenue deterioration (>10% YoY decline again), guidance cuts, or services gross-margin compression accelerating — confirming structural share loss rather than a transient digestion period; also a break below the buyback-supported range (~$70 average repurchase price) on volume.

evidence_refs.why: Core problem: operating income -11.7% YoY with opex (+11.3%) growing far faster than revenue (+3.1%) — negative operating leverage caps near-term rerating odds
Current deferred revenue up to $396.7M from $352.6M signals durable maintenance/recurring demand that supports the floor under estimates
$1.19B cash/investments, no debt, $225.5M six-month OCF — substantial downside protection at a price already 40% off highs
$277.2M remaining authorization (~4.5% of market cap) with demonstrated execution at avg $70.13 provides an active bid below current price
Product revenue -9.8% YoY confirms the demand deceleration that caused the drawdown; needs reversal evidence before committing capital
R&D +20.6% YoY and rising SBC ($118.6M unrecognized) mean even stable revenue may not restore margin trajectory quickly

trades.thesis: Barnes Group enters the window deeply derated (-51% from 1y high) despite fundamentally solid continuing operations: Q3 sales +16% y/y, Industrial operating profit up ~150% y/y, gross margin +400bps, and a balance sheet transformed by the BDNA sale ($230M cash, $464M unused revolver, 1.48x leverage vs 3.25x covenant). However, the bull case lacks a credible near-term rerating mechanism within 90 days: the Männer acquisition (closed Oct 31, 2013) adds integration risk and $202M of debt with purchase accounting incomplete; a ~$13M Tax Court payment is due in Q4; $54.3M of converts become putable March 15, 2014; Aerospace operating profit halved y/y on an $8.6M inventory charge; and 9M operating cash flow collapsed to $12.6M (albeit distorted by $95.7M of BDNA-gain tax payments). The deep drawdown suggests the market is already pricing Aerospace aftermarket weakness and deal execution risk, providing some valuation support, but cheapness plus deleveraging alone has not produced a rerating catalyst. Earnings quality is mixed — headline net income is dominated by the one-time $194M BDNA gain while continuing-ops income declined 13.4% for nine months. Net: tolerable downside given liquidity strength, but insufficient near-term upside mechanism to underwrite a long.
trades.catalyst: Q4/full-year 2013 earnings report (late Jan/Feb 2014) providing first Männer contribution data and normalized cash flow; potential further buybacks under the ~2.65M-share remaining authorization; resolution of the Second Circuit tax appeal posture by the Nov 18, 2013 deadline.
trades.invalidation: Q4 2013 results showing continued Aerospace margin erosion, weak Männer initial contribution, or guidance below expectations; any sign the March 2014 convert put plus acquisition debt strains liquidity; further unexplained share-price deterioration suggesting an undisclosed fundamental problem.

evidence_refs.why: Q3 sales +16% y/y and 9M +19% show genuine top-line momentum in the continuing portfolio, the core requirement for any rerating thesis.
Industrial operating profit more than doubled y/y ($20.9M vs $8.4M), offsetting Aerospace deterioration and supporting the growth narrative.
Aerospace operating profit halved y/y including an $8.6M inventory charge — a real quality-of-earnings concern that likely explains part of the ~51% drawdown and caps upside.

€281M acquisition closed Oct 31, 2013 with new risk factors citing integration risk, management distraction, and added indebtedness — an unproven capital deployment that raises execution uncertainty in the forecast window.
Dated Nov 18, 2013 deadline with ~$13M Q4 cash payment and Second Circuit appeal — a known, modest-sized overhang rather than a positive catalyst.
$54.3M of 3.375% converts putable at par March 15, 2014 (within the 90-day window) — a near-term claim on cash just as $202M was deployed for Männer.
$464.4M unused revolver (extended to 2018) and 1.48x leverage vs 3.25x covenant make the convert put and tax payment comfortably fundable; downside is liquidity-constrained, not solvency-constrained.
2.35M shares repurchased YTD with more planned signals shareholder-friendly capital allocation, but buybacks alone are not a rerating mechanism.

trades.thesis: Best Buy (inferred from FY2014 10-K, fiscal year ended 2014-02-01) is a deep-turnaround retail situation trading ~41% below its 1-year high at ~$16.45. The filings show a credible, partially de-risked Renew Blue execution story rather than mere cheapness: (1) return to profitability from continuing operations ($689M net earnings, $1.98 diluted EPS) after a FY2013 burdened by $822M goodwill impairments and $414M restructuring, with FY2014 restructuring down to $159M and no goodwill impairment — the P&L reset is largely complete; (2) material balance-sheet repair: cash up to $2.7B from $1.8B, debt reduced to $1,657M, current ratio 1.4 vs 1.1, $1.1B operating cash flow with capex cut to $547M; (3) unqualified auditor opinions on both financials and ICFR with no material weaknesses; (4) two of three rating agencies (Fitch BB-, S&P BB) moved outlooks from Negative to Stable, validating the credit inflection despite Moody's Negative outlook; (5) tangible transformation execution — ship-from-store at >1,400 locations, 1,400 Samsung and 600 Windows stores-within-a-store, phase-1 space optimization, plus completed portfolio pruning (Europe JV, mindSHIFT). The rerating mechanism is a scheduled, near-term catalyst: Q1 FY2015 earnings (~late May 2014) and the June 10 annual meeting, where stabilization of domestic comps and gross margin against easy post-impairment comparisons could force a re-rating of a stock priced for structural decline. The -41% drawdown embeds substantial pessimism, so even modest fundamental beats carry outsized upside, while the repaired balance sheet ($2.7B cash, reduced debt) makes the classic retail-turnaround failure mode (vendor credit tightening) less imminent. This is a genuine long candidate, not a value trap on cheapness alone — but conviction is capped by still-negative comps, gross margin at a five-year low (22.8%), and extreme supplier concentration (top 5 vendors ~45% of purchases, no long-term contracts).
trades.catalyst: Q1 FY2015 earnings report (~late May 2014) as the nearest hard catalyst: first full quarter to demonstrate whether Renew Blue cost savings and omnichannel initiatives (ship-from-store, vendor stores-within-a-store) can stabilize comps and gross margin; secondary: April proxy/June 10 annual meeting for capital-allocation signals given the untouched $4.0B buyback authorization.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q1 FY2015 results (due within the 90-day window) show continued domestic comp declines with further gross-margin erosion, or if vendors tighten payment terms/credit limits (the 10-K's explicitly flagged liquidity risk), or if Moody's downgrades from Baa2, re-opening the financing-cost spiral. A break back toward the 52-week lows on fundamental deterioration would confirm failure.

evidence_refs.why: $1.1B operating cash flow, cash up to $2.7B, capex cut to $547M, debt reduced to $1,657M — balance-sheet repair materially lowers the vendor-credit/financing tail risk that defines the bear case for this retailer.

Restructuring charges fell to $159M from $822M goodwill impairment + $414M restructuring in FY2013 with no FY2014 goodwill impairment — the P&L reset is largely behind, so year-over-year earnings comparisons become easier and a rerating base is established.
Unqualified ICFR and financial-statement opinions with no material weaknesses reduce the risk that reported turnaround progress is an accounting artifact.

Executed Renew Blue milestones (ship-from-store >1,400 stores, 1,400 Samsung + 600 Windows shops-in-shop, phase-1 space optimization) provide concrete, verifiable evidence the turnaround strategy is being implemented, not just promised.
Fitch (BB-) and S&P (BB) moved outlooks from Negative to Stable — external validation that the credit trajectory has inflected, partially offsetting Moody's Negative outlook.
Gross margin fell to 22.8% (five-year low) on price investment and promotion, and comps were negative — the core operating thesis is not yet proven and caps conviction.
Top 5 vendors ~45% of purchases with no long-term contracts; vendor tightening of terms is the principal tail scenario that could force financing and break the thesis.

trades.thesis: Ultra Clean-style semicap supplier shows a genuine operating inflection in the just-filed Q1 FY2014 10-Q: sales +43.5% YoY to $144.2M, gross margin up ~240bp to 16.2%, operating income up to $9.2M from $0.6M on flat opex, and a swing to $7.1M net income ($0.24 diluted). At $8.38 with ~29.4M shares (~$247M market cap) and only modest net debt ($74.3M cash vs ~$63.7M borrowings), the stock trades at a high-single-digit multiple of run-rate earnings after a -44% drawdown from its 1-year high — the market is pricing cyclicality/concentration, not the current earnings power. The credible near-term rerating mechanism is continuation of the beat trajectory into the next quarterly report within the 90-day window, which would force upward revisions off a depressed base. Downside looks tolerable: positive FCF (~$3.5M), management's 12-month liquidity assertion, and a balance sheet roughly neutral net of cash cushion a stock already heavily de-rated. That said, this is a conditional candidate, not a high-conviction one: operating cash flow fell to $4.0M from $16.3M on AR/inventory builds (finished goods nearly tripled) with a $1.4M one-time tax benefit flattering EPS, top-three customers are 79% of sales and ~76% of AR, revolver draws rose $11M under a blanket-lien facility with covenant consent requirements, the COO resigned in March, and $76.4M of goodwill/intangibles sits as an impairment overhang. Cheapness plus inflection earns a candidacy; earnings-quality and concentration risks keep position-sizing discipline and probabilities near base rates.
trades.catalyst: Next quarterly report (Q2 FY2014, due ~early August 2014, inside the 90-day window): if sales/margins hold near Q1 levels, trailing EPS annualizes to roughly $0.90+ against an $8.38 price (~9x), giving a concrete re-rating trigger; secondary support from continued debt paydown out of free cash flow.
trades.invalidation: Any sign the Q1 surge is not durable: guidance/backlog softness, order pushouts from Lam/AMAT/ASM, further AR/inventory build without revenue follow-through, covenant pressure requiring lender consent for financing, or a break below the post-drawdown trading range on heavy volume would invalidate the re-rating setup.

evidence_refs.why: Operating income jumped to $9.2M from $0.6M on flat opex — the core of the earnings-inflection thesis
+43.5% YoY sales to $144.2M confirms demand recovery, not just margin noise
OCF fell to $4.0M vs $16.3M despite higher income; working-capital build and one-time tax benefit cap confidence in earnings quality
Top three customers = 79% of sales / ~76% of AR (Lam, AMAT, ASM); single largest tail-risk to the thesis
$74.3M cash vs ~$63.7M total debt plus positive FCF supports balance-sheet floor and tolerable downside
~29.4M shares outstanding anchors valuation math (~$247M market cap vs ~$0.24 quarterly diluted EPS)
$55.9M goodwill impairment overhang if market cap stays below book equity — limits upside multiple

trades.thesis: MacroGenics enters the window fundamentally sound but without a credible 90-day rerating mechanism. Positives are real: $198.7M cash (no debt) funding the pipeline into 2017, a fresh $76.7M net follow-on, and external validation via Servier's Q1'14 MGD006 option exercise ($15.0M license fee + $5.0M IND milestone) plus positive Q1 operating cash flow (+$5.9M, though entirely collaboration-payment-driven). However, the stock trades ~50% below its 1-year high and well below the $36.50 follow-on price, signaling broken post-IPO momentum and an active seller overhang. Remaining catalysts (Servier MGD007/third-DART options, Gilead selections worth $7.5-15M+) carry undisclosed timing, one Gilead option has already expired unexercised, and the January 2014 prospective extension of Servier upfront recognition explicitly signals slower-than-planned development. With ~$7/share cash against a ~$550M market cap, R&D spend up ~45% YoY, and episodic milestone-dependent economics, cheapness on cash alone does not clear the bar for a long candidate; the setup warrants monitoring for a dated catalyst rather than initiation.
trades.catalyst: Potential further Servier DART option exercises (MGD007 / third molecule) or Gilead selections bringing $5-15M+ license fees, plus any Phase 3 margetuximab enrollment/data-timing updates; none confirmed within the 90-day window.
trades.invalidation: Thesis flips positive if Servier exercises the MGD007/third-molecule option or Gilead selects a DART program with disclosed payment/timing, or if margetuximab Phase 3 hits an announced enrollment/data milestone; thesis turns bearish if cash burn accelerates materially above run-rate or another collaboration timeline slips.

evidence_refs.why: $198.7M cash, no debt, runway into 2017 caps financing-risk downside over the forecast window
Q1'14 Servier option exercise ($15M) plus $5M IND milestone validates the DART platform but is already public/stale as a rerating driver
Jan 2014 prospective extension of upfront recognition signals development timelines slipping — undermines near-term catalyst density
One Gilead option period already lapsed without exercise; remaining options/milestones have undisclosed timing, so no bankable 90-day trigger
~97.5M of 125M authorized shares unissued plus recent $36.50 follow-on vs $20.16 price create persistent dilution/overhang pressure

trades.thesis: Advanced Energy shows genuine GAAP operating momentum (Q1 2014 sales +26% to $140.9M, operating income more than doubled to $16.9M, OCF $6.8M vs $0.5M) and a solid net-cash balance sheet ($122.7M cash+securities vs $15.1M debt), yet the stock sits ~40% below its 1-year high at $16.91. The core problem is forward-looking: management itself guides to a 'slight pause' in semiconductor investments with H2 memory demand unclear (NAND oversupply), the Inverters SBU swung to a $6.3M operating loss, backlog slipped to $127.5M, and non-semi markets fell 11%. Earnings quality caveats compound this: modest OCF conversion (~46% of NI on an $11.5M AR build), $173M goodwill (~26% of assets) concentrated in a Refusol deal showing $91.5M goodwill against negative identifiable net assets amid an unresolved Stuttgart court purchase-price dispute, prior PV Powered impairments signaling inverter-market weakness, and long-tail 5-10 year warranties with elevated accruals. With no credible near-term rerating catalyst (the dispute resolution and earnout determination are small and uncertain, and the next print will likely confirm the guided semi pause), cheapness (~12x run-rate EPS) alone does not clear the bar for a long candidate. The -40% drawdown suggests substantial pessimism is already priced, limiting expected downside, so the name merits monitoring for evidence that the semi pause is shallower than guided or that Precision Power momentum offsets it.
trades.catalyst: No high-conviction near-term catalyst identified: potential upside surprises would be better-than-feared semi orders despite the guided pause, or favorable resolution of the Refusol Stuttgart court dispute (small cash impact); next quarterly report (~late July 2014) is the main re-rating window.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidates if Q2 2014 results confirm the guided semi pause (sequential sales decline, further backlog erosion) or if Inverters losses widen / goodwill impairment signals emerge from the Refusol exposure.

evidence_refs.why: Management's own MD&A flags a near-term semiconductor investment pause and unclear H2 memory demand — directly undermines the near-term rerating mechanism required for a long candidate.
Inverters SBU swung to a $6.3M operating loss with backlog declining, offsetting Precision Power strength and adding segment-level downside risk.
Operating income more than doubled YoY ($16.9M vs $7.7M) with opex leverage — genuine fundamental momentum that keeps the name on the watch list rather than rejected.
$122.7M cash+securities vs $15.1M debt and $476M equity limits balance-sheet tail risk despite the -40% drawdown.
$91.5M goodwill against negative identifiable net assets plus an unresolved Stuttgart court dispute adds an unquantified contingent risk to earnings quality.

trades.thesis: Halozyme (inferred from rHuPH20/Hylenex/Roche SC disclosures) trades at $7.37, -58% from its 1-year high, after a February 2014 equity raise ($107.7M net at $13.00) left ~$160M cash+securities versus ~$17.6M quarterly operating burn — roughly 2 years of runway, so financing risk is muted over a 90-day horizon. A credible but unproven rerating mechanism exists: first royalties ($0.8M) and bulk rHuPH20 sales following Roche's EU approvals of Herceptin SC (Aug 2013) and MabThera SC (Mar 2014), plus one product candidate pending U.S. approval. However, the bear case is substantive: net loss widened to $(26.5)M, operating cash burn rose 63% YoY, collaborative revenue collapsed ($2.6M vs $10.3M), two collaborations were terminated in early 2014 (ViroPharma, Intrexon), remaining partners hold 30-day termination rights, and the headline product-sales surge is partly inflated by a Dec 2013 revenue-recognition change. Cheapness plus a funded runway is not enough; the rerating driver (royalty ramp, FDA decision) lacks a disclosed dated trigger within the window, and momentum/negative operating trajectory argue against initiating now.
trades.catalyst: Potential U.S. regulatory decision on the submitted product candidate (Baxter HyQvia) plus continued royalty ramp from Roche's 2013–14 EU subcutaneous approvals (Herceptin SC, MabThera SC); neither has a disclosed dated timeline in the filings, which caps conviction.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if the U.S. approval is delayed or rejected, if another collaborator terminates, or if Q2 results reveal that ex-rev-rec-change product growth is decelerating while burn continues to widen against covenant-constrained debt.

evidence_refs.why: Product sales $8.6M vs $1.5M YoY plus first royalties ($0.8M) evidence an emerging commercial/royalty model anchored to Roche EU SC approvals — the core of any rerating thesis.
$107.7M net raise leaves ~$160M cash+securities vs ~$17.6M quarterly burn (~2yr runway), removing near-term financing/dilution risk and making downside over 90 days more tolerable.
Two collaborations already terminated in early 2014 (ViroPharma, Intrexon) and remaining partners can exit on 30 days' notice — active partner attrition undermines the collaboration-value narrative.
Net loss widened to $(26.5)M with operating burn up 63% YoY; the business is moving away from profitability even as revenue mix shifts, limiting fundamental support for the stock.

Hylenex revenue recognition change effective 12/31/2013 flatters YoY product-sales growth; underlying demand cannot be separated from the accounting change in supplied excerpts, discounting the 'commercial inflection' claim.
One product candidate is under U.S. regulatory review — a genuine near-term binary catalyst, but no PDUFA date is disclosed, so timing risk within the 90-day window is material.

trades.thesis: Veeva trades at $20.75, ~55% below its 1-year high and ~21% below the March 2014 follow-on price of $26.35, despite fundamentals that are rare among 2014 cloud names: Q1 FY2015 revenue +56% YoY ($66.7M) with subscription revenue +74%, GAAP profitability (net income $7.2M), operating cash flow of $18.1M (~2.5x net income), deferred revenue building $7.5M sequentially to $74.9M, and a debt-free balance sheet with $345.5M in cash/investments (~13% of the ~$2.6B market cap). At roughly 8–9x forward EV/revenue for 55%+ growth with real GAAP margins, valuation is undemanding versus cloud comps of the era. The drawdown appears driven by technical/supply factors — the mostly-secondary follow-on (12.41M of 13.8M shares sold by insiders) and the June 16, 2014 lockup expiration (~88M shares eligible) — rather than fundamental deterioration. The bear case is governance (dual-class, 95.9% Class B voting power), rising opex growth outpacing revenue, EGC disclosure exemptions, and salesforce.com purchase commitments (~$496.7M through 2025). Cheapness alone is insufficient, but here cheapness coincides with accelerating fundamentals and an identifiable supply-clearing event within the forecast window, giving a credible rerating mechanism into the September Q2 print.
trades.catalyst: Post-lockup supply absorption after June 16, 2014 followed by Q2 FY2015 earnings (early September) where continued ~50%+ subscription growth and deferred revenue build could re-anchor the multiple toward the $26.35 offering reference price; no other dated catalysts appear in the filing.
trades.invalidation: Failure of the stock to stabilize within 2–4 weeks after the June 16 lockup expiration (sustained trade below ~$18–19), or Q2 FY2015 results showing subscription growth decelerating materially below ~50% YoY or deferred revenue stagnation — either would break the growth-plus-quality rerating mechanism.

evidence_refs.why: GAAP-profitable hypergrowth SaaS with OCF ~2.5x net income confirms earnings quality, differentiating VEEVA from unprofitable peers and supporting a durable premium multiple.
$7.5M sequential deferred revenue build on non-cancellable subscriptions provides forward revenue visibility that underpins the rerating thesis.
$345.5M cash/investments and zero debt (~13% of market cap) provide downside cushion and eliminate financing risk.
12.41M of 13.8M follow-on shares were secondary at $26.35; with the stock at $20.75 much insider supply has already cleared, weakening the remaining overhang argument.
95.9% Class B voting control entrenches management and caps any takeover/control-premium path; a real but non-blocking discount factor.
