S&M (+67%) and G&A (+72%) growing faster than revenue limits near-term margin expansion, tempering how fast operating leverage can drive the rerating.

trades.thesis: The name (Nevada-domiciled workers' comp insurer, ~$13.92 pre-cutoff, -41% from 1Y high) screens statistically cheap — roughly 0.65-0.70x book (equity ~$645M vs ~31.5M shares) — with genuinely improving core operations: NPE +7.9%/+10.4% (Q/YTD), underwriting swung to income, expense leverage, positive net rate, and solid H1 operating cash flow of $78.1M. However, the headline Q2 beat is heavily flattered by $29.6M of one-time LPT-related estimate changes; core net income was only $14.6M vs $9.9M. Critically, there is no credible near-term rerating mechanism: no buyback activity, no guidance raise, no M&A or regulatory catalysts disclosed, while gross premium growth is sluggish (+1.9% Q), investment yields are falling (tax-equivalent 3.9%), California concentration exceeds half the book, cumulative trauma claims are trending adversely, and assigned-risk business showed adverse development. The 41% drawdown suggests the market already discounts reserve-quality skepticism that this filing does not fully dispel. Cheapness plus improving-but-low-quality earnings without a dated catalyst argues for monitoring rather than initiating; base rates for deep-value micro/small-cap insurers without catalysts show wide dispersion and only mild positive drift.
trades.catalyst: No dated near-term catalyst identified. Potential soft catalysts: follow-through on new California pricing options effective June 1, 2014 (territorial multipliers/multiple subsidiaries) supporting rate-driven premium growth, possible further favorable LPT true-ups on paid-loss trends, and any initiation of buybacks given historical precedent (~43% treasury position) — none committed in the filing.
trades.invalidation: Thesis invalidated if Q3 2014 results show reversal of LPT-related gains or renewed adverse development outside the LPT agreement, if California pricing initiatives fail to sustain net rate/in-force growth, or if cumulative trauma claim cost trends accelerate into accident-year loss picks; also any covenant stress around the December 2014 $10M amortization.

evidence_refs.why: $29.6M of Q2 net income from one-time LPT adjustments vs core net income of only $14.6M caps confidence that the earnings inflection is durable enough to force a rerating.
NPE +7.9%/+10.4% with positive net rate (+2.6% overall, +4.3% CA) and expense leverage shows genuine underlying operating improvement beneath the noise.
Rising cumulative trauma claims and upward medical/indemnity cost per claim in current accident year estimates offset the favorable prior-period narrative and support caution on reserve adequacy.

$10M Dec-2014 and $60M Dec-2015 facility amortization against modest holdco cash creates a known capital event inside/outside the window; manageable ($78.1M H1 OCF) but limits buyback optionality as a catalyst.
>50% of business from California (60% of in-force premiums) concentrates both the pricing-opportunity upside and the regulatory/cycle downside of the thesis.
Adverse prior-year development on assigned risk coexisting with large favorable LPT adjustments signals mixed reserve adequacy across books, tempering trust in headline releases.

trades.thesis: 8x8 (EGHT, $6.86, -43% from 1-year high) pairs genuine top-line momentum — Q2 FY15 revenue +29% YoY to a record $39.6M, service revenue +30%, customers +16.6% to ~40,400, ARPU +12% to $299/month, churn 0.9% — with a fortress balance sheet ($185.6M cash+ST investments, no debt, total liabilities just $22.9M, ~$6.1M six-month FCF). At ~$614M market cap, net cash is roughly 30% of the equity value, cushioning downside. The de-rate appears driven by deteriorating operating leverage (S&M +41% YoY to 49% of revenue; six-month operating income halved to $3.0M from $5.3M), ~20% share dilution, doubling SBC, and earnings-quality noise (one-time $1.0M patent-sale gain inside operating income; flat OCF despite growth; AR outpacing revenue; deferred revenue shrinking). This is not cheapness alone: the rerating mechanism is that retention/ARPU/mid-market mix (41% vs 35% of service revenue) are all improving while the stock prices in stagnation — if management demonstrates expense discipline at the upcoming Q3 print (late Jan 2015, inside the window), the growth-plus-net-cash profile supports multiple recovery. Skepticism is warranted: no dated catalyst is disclosed beyond the routine earnings cycle, margins are moving the wrong way, and dilution/SBC erode per-share value, so position sizing should reflect a modest edge rather than conviction.
trades.catalyst: Q3 FY2015 earnings report (expected late January 2015, within the 90-day window): if it shows sequential S&M discipline or margin stabilization alongside sustained ~25-30% service revenue growth and sub-1% churn, the market can begin re-rating the multiple off the -43% drawdown; secondary support from the favorable trajectory of the USPTO reexamination invalidating the '722 patent in the Bear Creek suit.
trades.invalidation: Q3 FY2015 results showing S&M still growing faster than revenue with further six-month operating income decline, deferred revenue continuing to shrink, or AR growth again outpacing revenue would confirm structurally declining unit economics; additionally, any adverse turn in the Bear Creek litigation or acceleration of dilution above current pace invalidates the setup.

evidence_refs.why: Record $39.6M revenue, +29% YoY, with service revenue +29.8% — demand momentum intact despite the stock's -43% drawdown, underpinning a rerating thesis.
0.9% monthly revenue churn (second straight quarter sub-1%) plus ARPU +12% to $299 evidences durable recurring-revenue quality that supports eventual margin recovery.
$185.6M cash/investments (~$2.1/share, ~30% of market cap), no debt, positive FCF — bounds downside risk and funds the investment cycle without financing dependence.
Six-month operating income halved to $3.0M from $5.3M — the core bear case; without an operating-leverage inflection the rerating thesis fails.
~20% share count expansion and 6.8M pool increase dilute per-share economics and cap upside; a key discount driver.
$1.0M one-time patent-sale gain flatters Q2 operating income — reported profitability overstates run-rate earnings.
USPTO rejected all claims of the '722 patent underlying the Bear Creek suit — potential removal of a lingering legal overhang.

trades.thesis: Micro-cap manufacturer trading ~54% below its 1-year high ($4.60) with genuinely improving operations: Q3 sales +4.1%, operating income +15.6% (9M +32.2%), gross margin expansion, overhead leverage, and growth across all three segments. The balance sheet is exceptionally clean — zero debt, $7.05M cash, $2.43M appreciated marketable securities, 16:1 current ratio, undrawn $3.5M revolver — and management continues retiring shares via buybacks. However, this is a quality-of-earnings-discounted story, not a momentum one: 9M operating cash flow collapsed to $973K from $5.35M on AR/prepaid builds, $409K of pre-tax income came from non-operating investment gains, Harmony JV equity income fell sharply in Q3, and WIP inventory jumped 75%. Critically, no dated near-term catalyst exists in any filing: no guidance, no named contracts or launches, and the buyback capacity remaining ($1.56M) is too small relative to float to force a rerate. Cheapness plus a strong balance sheet limits downside but does not constitute a rerating mechanism within 90 days. The stock's -54% drawdown suggests the market has already discounted the earnings-quality concerns; without a catalyst, mean reversion depends on passive drift and the next 10-K, which falls mostly beyond the window.
trades.catalyst: None dated or disclosed. Potential future rerating drivers would be Q4 cash-flow normalization validating the working-capital build as timing-related, continued buyback execution at depressed prices, or a take-out of the illiquid micro-cap at a multiple of book — none are near-term or verifiable from filings known at cutoff.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 results show the working-capital build is structural rather than timing (continued OCF weakness), if WIP keeps rising without corresponding finished-goods conversion and shipments, or if Q3's near-zero Harmony JV equity income persists — any of which would convert 'watch' into a reject; conversely, evidence of normalized cash conversion would upgrade it toward a value candidate.

evidence_refs.why: Q3 operating income +15.6% and 9M +32.2% on all three segments growing sales shows genuine operating leverage, the core fundamental support
9M OCF collapsed to $973K from $5.35M on AR/prepaid builds — a material earnings-quality divergence from reported net income growth that undermines conviction in the fundamental story
Debt-free balance sheet with $7.05M cash, $2.43M securities, 16:1 current ratio and undrawn $3.5M revolver makes insolvency/distress risk remote, capping downside tail
Ongoing retired-share buybacks ($2.03M YTD, $1.56M remaining authorization) provide a slow per-share accretion floor but are too small to be a rerating catalyst
$409K of 9M pre-tax income from non-operating investment gains plus sharply declining Harmony JV equity income ($22K vs $101K in Q3) means headline EPS overstates run-rate operating power
WIP inventory up 75% YoY alongside the receivables build is an early warning that the working-capital drag may reflect demand/production mismatch rather than pure timing

trades.thesis: Sturm Ruger screens as a classic cyclical destocking trough rather than structural impairment. The filing shows Q3 sales -43% YoY, gross margin compressed to 24.1% from 36.8%, backlog down from 1.9M to 825K units, and OCF down to $31M from $84M — yet management's own data show underlying consumer demand down only ~3% (NICS-adjusted) versus -44% distributor sell-through, indicating the collapse is predominantly channel inventory correction, which is inherently mean-reverting once distributors reach reasonable levels. The stock is already down ~42% from its 1-year high, pricing substantial pessimism; at ~$31 with roughly 19M shares outstanding, EV is well under 5x annualized trough EBITDA for a debt-free franchise. The feared Q4 items are known and dated: ~$40M pension settlement expense (mostly non-operating, ~$8M cash) terminates a legacy obligation permanently, and the dividend was preemptively cut to $0.14 preserving cash. A credible rerating mechanism exists: the AR-556 launched end-September at a competitive price point with shipments ramping into Q4/Q1, positioning the company to recapture share in the largest category as destocking abates. Downside is tolerable given zero debt, $28.1M cash, unused $40M revolver, unencumbered assets, and cost actions already taken (production -36%, incentive comp -89%). This is a deep-value cyclical turn setup, not a cheapness-only bet: the catalyst path runs through Q4 earnings demonstrating destocking completion and AR-556 traction, with the one-time pension charge absorbed and guided.
trades.catalyst: Q4/full-year 2014 earnings report (~late Feb 2015, inside the 90-day window): first quarter with AR-556 volume shipments, evidence that distributor destocking has abated (orders stabilizing against a -3% underlying demand base), and clear demonstration that the ~$40M pension settlement charge is non-recurring — enabling the market to re-focus on normalized mid-cycle earnings power at ~4x EV/EBITDA rather than trough optics.
trades.invalidation: Q4-to-date order data or the February earnings report showing continued double-digit order declines, further backlog erosion, accelerating market-share loss to discounting competitors, or cash falling materially below ~$20M (forcing dividend elimination or revolver draw) would invalidate the trough thesis; also watch failure to renew the $40M revolver ahead of its June 15, 2015 termination.

evidence_refs.why: Quantifies the severity of the drawdown driver (-43% sales, -44% sell-through) that is already reflected in a -42% stock drawdown

Management's own disclosure that consumer demand fell only ~3% (NICS-adjusted) versus -44% sell-through identifies the decline as primarily transitory channel destocking, not end-demand destruction — the core of the contrarian case
AR-556 launched end of September with limited Q3 shipments; ramp into Q4/Q1 provides a concrete volume recovery mechanism in the entry-level modern sporting rifle segment
~$40M Q4 income statement expense is known, dated, and non-cash-heavy (~$8M cash); a disclosed one-time item removes an overhang and de-risks the next print rather than creating surprise risk
Debt-free balance sheet, covenant compliance, unused $40M revolver, and unencumbered assets make forced deleveraging/distressed outcomes unlikely during the trough
Orders -65% and backlog down 1.1M units cap near-term revenue visibility and are the principal bearish counterweight; also flags negative FCF pressure
Dividend cut to $0.14 from $0.45 confirms management sees prolonged weakness — supports capital preservation but signals no near-term inflection is guaranteed

trades.thesis: Amkor (AMKR, ~$5.55, -51% from 1y high) shows quote-grounded operating inflection: Q3'14 net sales +5.8% YoY to $812.8M, gross margin 18.8% vs 18.4%, operating income +29.6% to $75.2M, and nine-month net income attributable to Amkor of $117.3M vs $68.5M. Deleveraging is real (short-term debt cut to $10M, $140M LT repaid, converts converted), near-term maturities are trivial ($5M 2014/2015), and undrawn capacity (~$435M revolvers/term facilities) plus management's twelve-month sufficiency assertion make the balance sheet serviceable. The deep drawdown appears largely explained by the October 2014 Tessera judgment ($113M + $15M pre-judgment interest, 10% post-judgment interest, stayed via appeal bond) — a ~$128M+ contingent claim against $485.6M cash that is painful but absorbable, and partially pre-accrued ($43.3M royalties). A dated near-term catalyst exists: Q4 2014 exercise window to raise J-Devices ownership to 66%, with a path to 80% consolidation in 2015 when governance restrictions lapse. Offsets that cap conviction: negative trailing FCF ($405.7M OCF vs $442.3M capex), ~$675M 2014 capex plan, working-capital build (payables $626.6M vs $365.3M), one-time gains inflating reported income (~$9.2M J-Devices sale gain), founder control (~58% Kim family) with dormant buyback, and ERP/integration control risk. Net: improving fundamentals plus a credible rerating mechanism (J-Devices consolidation, Tessera overhang resolution) at a distressed price justify a modest-conviction long candidate, not a high-conviction one.
trades.catalyst: Q4 2014 exercise window for options to raise J-Devices ownership to 66% (path to 80% consolidation in 2015, when governance restrictions lapse), plus continued operating leverage from advanced-packaging smartphone demand; any favorable Tessera appeal development would remove the principal overhang.
trades.invalidation: Adverse Tessera appeal outcome requiring near-term cash payment beyond accruals, Q4 guidance showing margin compression from the ~$675M capex program, or further cash/working-capital deterioration that forces reliance on external financing.

evidence_refs.why: Quote-grounded +29.6% YoY operating income growth with SG&A leverage evidences a genuine fundamental inflection, not just headline revenue.
October 2014 $113M+$15M judgment at 10% post-judgment interest is the key bearish overhang; sized against $485.6M cash and $435M undrawn facilities it is absorbable but caps conviction.
Q4 2014 exercisable option to raise J-Devices to 66% (80% in 2015) provides a dated, funded near-term event with consolidation upside.
Payables jump to $626.6M and cash decline to $485.6M flag working-capital strain that tempers the earnings-improvement thesis.
Staged 60%→66%→80% control path with consolidation at 80% is a credible rerating mechanism, though cash-pay exercise prices and founder control (~58% Kim family) limit float and re-rating speed.

trades.thesis: Beaten-down recently-IPO'd SaaS communications company trading at roughly $0.9B market cap (~68.1M shares x $13.07) against ~$215M annualized revenue growing 36% YoY — approximately 1.1x EV/Sales after netting $149.4M cash/ST investments against $27.2M debt. The rerating mechanism is credible: fundamentals are accelerating (gross margin ~66% and rising, deferred revenue +$6.9M YTD, operating cash burn cut from $(20.6)M to $(7.1)M), while the stock's -44% drawdown from its 1-year high suggests expectations have been fully reset after post-IPO/secondary lockup supply. Liquidity risk is minimal ($149M cash, covenant compliance, management runway assertion), so the main risks are sentiment-based rather than solvency-based. Cheapness alone would not suffice, but here cheapness coincides with intact hyper-growth and improving unit economics — a classic setup for multiple recovery in a high-growth SaaS name once overhang clears. Counterweights: GAAP losses are widening ($(38.2)M nine-month), SBC doubled to $11.3M, part of the burn improvement is an $11.3M accrued-liability build, and founder-controlled dual-class governance caps strategic alternatives. Position sizing should reflect small-cap beta and the possibility that loss-making SaaS stays out of favor.
trades.catalyst: Q4/full-year 2014 results (early 2015) showing sustained ~35%+ revenue growth and continued burn reduction against a depressed ~1x EV/S multiple; any upward revision or reaffirmation of the growth trajectory could trigger a sharp rerating given the stock's 44% drawdown and thin float dynamics typical of recent dual-class SaaS IPOs.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 results show revenue growth decelerating below ~30%, sequential deferred-revenue softness, or re-acceleration of cash burn; also invalidated by broader de-rating of unprofitable high-growth SaaS names or further insider selling into weakness.

evidence_refs.why: Q3 revenue +36% YoY to $56.9M with gross margin up to ~66% is the core demand/margin engine that justifies a premium multiple if sentiment recovers.
$149.4M cash and short-term investments vs only $27.2M debt removes balance-sheet risk as an overhang and makes dilutive emergency financing unlikely within the window.
Operating cash burn narrowed from $(20.6)M to $(7.1)M — evidence the growth-vs-cash tradeoff is improving, supporting a path-to-profitability narrative.
S&M growing faster than revenue and widening GAAP losses are the key bearish counterweight; they cap conviction and raise sensitivity to any growth deceleration print.
Founder-controlled dual-class structure with anti-takeover provisions limits acquisition/activist catalysts and minority-holder protection — a structural discount factor.
-44% from 1-year high at ~$13 leaves expectations reset; combined with ~$890M market cap (~1.1x forward EV/Sales on ~36% growth), valuation asymmetry favors upside.

trades.thesis: Prothena enters November 2014 well-capitalized ($306.2M cash, no debt, ~$11/share in cash against a $22.19 price) after a ~$117.4M June/July offering and $45M of Roche upfront/milestone payments. But the investment case fails the two-part test for a long candidate: (1) there is no credible near-term rerating mechanism — the extractions surface no dated NEOD001 data readout, regulatory filing, or scheduled milestone within the 90-day window, only contingent events; and (2) run-rate economics are deteriorating — Q3 operating loss widened to $(13.1)M YoY with R&D up ~64%, headline 9M profitability is entirely non-recurring Roche payments under the milestone method, and management itself expects 'substantial losses for the foreseeable future.' The -54% drawdown from the 1-year high reflects deflated NEOD001 expectations, not a mispricing with a near-term correction trigger. Cash coverage limits catastrophic downside, but a stock trading near its recent financing price with binary, unscheduled clinical catalysts offers no edge over SPY in 90 days.
trades.catalyst: No dated catalyst within the 90-day window is disclosed in the filings; the plausible rerating path is incremental — NEOD001 enrollment/progress updates or Roche PRX002 advancement news — with the real binary (NEOD001 efficacy data) sitting beyond the horizon.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would flip positive on a disclosed, dated NEOD001 data readout or regulatory milestone within the window, or on evidence that cash-per-share support plus trial progress attracts a strategic bid; it would turn bearish on accelerated burn guidance, supply disruption at Boehringer Ingelheim, or a new dilutive financing below the July 2014 ~$22.50 deal price.

evidence_refs.why: $306.2M cash vs ~27.4M shares outstanding (~$11/share) and zero debt provides a substantial downside cushion relative to the $22.19 price.
9M net income is entirely one-time Roche payments; Q3 operating loss widened to $(13.1)M as revenue lapses — run-rate economics are deeply loss-making.
Management explicitly expects substantial losses for the foreseeable future, confirming burn resumes and future financing/dilution risk.
~$117.4M raise at ~$22.50 in June/July 2014 anchors valuation near current price but also signals the cash will be spent, not returned.
Roche collaboration validates pipeline and funds development, but milestones are contingent rather than scheduled — no dated rerating event inside 90 days.
Complete dependence on Boehringer Ingelheim for clinical supply adds binary execution risk to an already binary clinical story.

trades.company: AMERICAN REALTY CAPITAL NEW YORK CITY REIT, INC.
trades.thesis: Reject. This is a freshly formed, externally managed non-traded NYC office REIT whose entire equity story depends on future deployment of a large undeployed cash balance through a conflicted sponsor platform. Within the 90-day window there is no credible rerating mechanism: GAAP results are immaterial and negative (Q3 net loss $(2.2)M on revenues of only $0.54M, with acquisition/transaction expense of $2.05M exceeding revenue), ~67% of assets are still cash, distributions are being funded partly from offering proceeds, and the only structural repricing event (NAV-based pricing after the second full fiscal quarter following April 24, 2016) lies well outside the horizon. The fee architecture is punitive — ~$36.7M cumulative offering costs (~10.7% of gross proceeds), up to 10% dealer manager compensation, related-party acquisition fees ($1.85M nine months), 4% property management fee, and 15% promotes — creating persistent per-share value leakage against NAV. Asset quality offers no offsetting margin of safety: just three properties totaling 132,552 SF with extreme tenant concentration (Cornell University 44.5%, TD Bank 18.6%), so outcomes are idiosyncratic rather than diversified. Cheapness cannot be assessed against fundamentals because reported book/NAV reflects $25.00 offer-price issuance, not market-validated value; the pro forma net income of $1.5M is a construction that excludes acquisition costs and assumes earlier closings. With a thin ~$4.1M/day tape, a governance-heavy structure, and a sponsor complex already under reputational stress in late 2014, the asymmetry over 90 days skews modestly negative versus SPY in a rising-rate environment pressuring rate-sensitive real estate vehicles. Base-rate skepticism toward newly listed, externally managed non-traded REIT structures supports standing aside.
trades.catalyst: None credible inside 90 days: deployment of the ~$207.7M cash pile into accretive acquisitions would be the only rerating lever, but each deal triggers related-party acquisition fees, and the structural repricing event (NAV-based share pricing/listing path) is contractually deferred beyond April 2016.
trades.invalidation: A rapid, fee-light deployment of the remaining ~$207.7M into leased NYC assets at cap rates well above the implied cost of capital, combined with an announced acceleration of the listing/NAV-pricing timeline or material advisor fee concessions, would invalidate the rejection and warrant re-review as a long candidate.

evidence_refs.why: Externally managed structure with advisor, property manager, dealer manager and SLP all under common control, plus up-to-10% dealer manager load, layered acquisition fees and 15% promotes — a persistent per-share value leakage that caps any rerating.
Q3 transaction costs ($2.0M) exceeded total revenues ($0.54M); GAAP earnings are negligible relative to fee drag, so there is no fundamental support for a premium to the $25 offer price.
Distributions are permitted from unlimited sources including IPO proceeds while operations are cash-negative — yield is artificial and offers no fundamental signal.
Cornell University alone is 44.5% of annualized straight-line rent across only three properties; idiosyncratic single-tenant risk dominates any portfolio-level thesis.

Fixed $25.00/$23.75 pricing persists until the NAV pricing date tied to a quarter after April 24, 2016 — the natural repricing event sits outside the 90-day window, removing the main mechanism for gap resolution.
The bull case rests entirely on pro forma net income ($1.5M) assuming full-period ownership and excluding acquisition costs — an unsupported claim that does not constitute a near-term catalyst.

trades.thesis: Vanda (VNDA, $9.31, -43% from 1y high, ~$390M market cap) is transitioning to commercial-stage: Q1 2015 delivered $22.15M of first-ever product revenue (HETLIOZ $7.5M + newly transferred Fanapt $14.7M), net loss narrowed to $10.2M from $26.5M, and operating cash flow turned positive (+$5.6M). With $134.3M in cash/securities, no debt, and a ~$90M annualized revenue run-rate, EV is roughly $255M (~2.8x run-rate sales) — not deeply cheap, but the -43% drawdown suggests meaningful pessimism is embedded. The credible near-term rerating mechanism is the European Commission's final decision on HETLIOZ, expected mid-2015 and therefore inside the 90-day window, following an April 2015 CHMP positive opinion — approval is the high-probability outcome and would add an EU revenue leg to an inflecting P&L. This is a catalyst-driven setup, not a cheapness-only thesis. The edge is modest, not large: the stock has already de-rated, Fanapt revenue is partly transition/channel-driven, and the market may treat EU approval as largely priced.
trades.catalyst: European Commission final decision on HETLIOZ expected mid-2015 (within the 90-day window) following the April 2015 CHMP positive opinion — a high-probability approval event that would open a second geography for the lead product and validate the commercial transition narrative.
trades.invalidation: EC decision delayed past the window or issued with restrictive labeling; Q2 Fanapt revenue showing transition/channel-stuffing reversal (AR collection failure given 80% AR concentration in three customers); equity financing announced; adverse development in the ANDA suits.

evidence_refs.why: Quote-grounded, dated catalyst inside the 90-day window; CHMP positive opinion already secured, making EC approval the high-probability base case and the primary rerating mechanism.
First commercial quarter with $22.15M product sales (~$90M annualized run-rate) against a ~$390M market cap and $134M cash — a genuine business-model inflection, not just cheapness.
$134.3M cash/securities, no debt, and positive operating cash flow (+$5.6M) limit financing-driven downside over the forecast horizon.
Top six customers = 95% of revenue and top three = 80% of AR; launch-quarter revenue quality is uncertain and could disappoint on follow-through.
ANDA challenges (Roxane trial Feb 2016; new Inventia suit) threaten the largest revenue component (Fanapt $14.7M/qtr) and cap the multiple the market will pay.
Management's explicit uncertainty about fund sufficiency plus the $25M milestone obligation and evergreen equity plan signal non-trivial dilution risk that tempers position sizing.

trades.thesis: OraSure-type small-cap diagnostics issuer at $5.33 (-49% from 1y high, ~$300M market cap vs ~$89.5M cash, no debt) shows a real but low-quality operating inflection: Q1 2015 revenue +15% YoY, operating loss narrowed to $(291)K from $(5.6)M, first modest GAAP profit ($113K). However, the improvement leans heavily on the AbbVie HCV co-promotion ramp ($3.3M Other revenue; ~12% of net revenues), whose $15M upfront payment is being recognized ratably and has already wound down from $7.4M to $4.1M deferred — this tailwind largely exhausts within the next quarter or two. Underlying economics remain cash-burning ($(6.6)M operating cash flow, ~-$7M FCF proxy), FX translation is eroding goodwill/comprehensive income, and the DNAG goodwill ($19.9M) faces its annual impairment test in fiscal Q3 — inside the 90-day window. A newly filed patent suit against Ancestry adds unquantifiable binary legal risk. Critically, there is no dated positive catalyst within 90 days: the first AbbVie milestone period ends Dec 31, 2015. With no credible near-term rerating mechanism, deteriorating revenue quality as the AbbVie annuity burns off, and a stock already de-rated ~50%, cheapness alone does not justify a long. Base rates for beaten-down micro/small-caps without near-term catalysts skew flat-to-negative on 90-day excess return.
trades.catalyst: No dated catalyst inside the 90-day window: the first AbbVie performance-based milestone period ends December 31, 2015 (~7+ months out), and the DNAG v. Ancestry patent suit outcome is unquantified and slow-moving. The nearest observable events are the fiscal Q3 DNAG goodwill impairment test (a risk event, not a positive catalyst) and the exhaustion of the AbbVie ratable revenue stream (a headwind).
trades.invalidation: Thesis would flip toward long if: (a) the company guides to sustained core product revenue growth excluding AbbVie ratable revenue, (b) operating cash flow turns positive for two consecutive quarters, or (c) a dated near-term catalyst emerges (e.g., Ancestry litigation settlement, new regulatory approvals, or accelerated AbbVie milestones). It would flip bearish on a Q3 goodwill impairment charge or disclosure that core HIV/HCV product revenues are declining ex-AbbVie.

evidence_refs.why: Genuine operating inflection (opex cut ~30% in S&M, gross margin up) supports a turnaround narrative, but the magnitude is small (-$291K op loss) relative to a ~$300M market cap.

Deferred AbbVie revenue fell $7.4M→$4.1M; the $15M payment recognized ratably is nearly exhausted, so the key driver of the Q1 GAAP profit inflection reverses within roughly two quarters — undermining the durability of the rerating thesis.
FX-driven goodwill decline and comprehensive loss show ongoing currency headwinds on the international/DNAG business; annual impairment test falls within the forecast window.
New patent suit against Ancestry is an unquantified binary legal overhang contradicting management's 'ordinary course' characterization; injunctive-relief outcomes are unpredictable.
~$89.5M cash, no debt, $105.6M working capital vs ~$300M market cap limits downside from financing/dilution risk, but does not by itself create upside.
-$6.6M quarterly operating cash flow despite reported net income signals weak earnings quality and continued underlying burn.
Nearest dated catalyst (first milestone period end Dec 31, 2015) sits outside the 90-day horizon, so no near-term rerating mechanism exists.

trades.thesis: Theravance Biopharma trades at $14.50, down ~58% from its 1-year high, yet the filings show a fundamentally stronger position than the chart implies: ~$275M of cash/marketable securities with zero debt against a modest market cap, leaving a large fraction of the share price backed by net cash. The Mylan collaboration provides third-party validation at a hard price anchor — a $30.0M equity investment at ~$18.918/share (a 10% premium to VWAP) plus a $15.0M upfront payment due in Q2 2015 and up to $220M in contingent milestones — all struck well above the current quote. The credible near-term rerating mechanism is the TD-4208 Phase 3 COPD program initiation expected in H2 2015 (inside the 90-day window), which is Mylan-funded until first NDA approval, plus ongoing VIBATIV Phase 3 SAB enrollment. Against this, the accounting specialist correctly flags that headline revenue is one-time license recognition ($19.1M of $20.4M) masking immaterial product sales ($1.28M/quarter vs generic vancomycin competition), and burn is accelerating ($56.5M operating cash use, +$11.7M YoY). Still, runway is ~4-5 quarters with management asserting ≥12 months, so dilution risk is not acute within the window. The setup is a deeply discounted, cash-rich clinical-stage name with a dated, partner-funded catalyst and an above-market insider-style entry price — cheapness alone would be insufficient, but here cheapness coincides with a specific catalyst and a validated price reference point. Position sizing should reflect binary-event risk inherent to Phase 3 starts and the possibility that the drawdown reflects sector-wide biotech de-rating rather than idiosyncratic value.
trades.catalyst: TD-4208 Phase 3 COPD program initiation expected H2 2015 (within the 90-day window), reinforced by receipt of the $15.0M Mylan upfront payment and continued VIBATIV Phase 3 SAB enrollment progress — each a visible, dated rerating trigger for a beaten-down name.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if TD-4208 Phase 3 initiation slips beyond the window or is delayed/restructured, if the company signals an equity raise before year-end (burn trajectory worsening against the 12-month runway assertion), or if VIBATIV commercial metrics deteriorate further — any of which would remove the rerating mechanism and expose the stock to its dilution/financing discount.

evidence_refs.why: $30M strategic equity purchase at ~$18.918/share, a 10% premium to VWAP, is informed-capital validation of the pipeline well above the current $14.50 price — the strongest single anchor for undervaluation.
Phase 3 COPD initiation expected in H2 2015 falls inside the 90-day forecast window and is Mylan-funded until first NDA approval — a concrete, dated rerating mechanism rather than vague optionality.

~$275M liquid assets, zero debt, and only $28.9M current liabilities mean enterprise value is a small fraction of market cap, compressing downside and removing financing-forced-selling risk inside the window.
Guards against over-crediting headline revenue: $19.1M of $20.4M is one-time license recognition with product sales of only $1.28M — the thesis rests on pipeline/cash, not commercial traction.
Operating burn rose to $(56.5)M in Q1 (+$11.7M YoY); even so, coverage is ~4-5 quarters, but it caps how far valuation can re-rate without further partnering or dilution.
VIBATIV competes against cheap generic vancomycin with only $1.28M quarterly sales — the commercial story cannot carry the stock; downside case relies on pipeline sentiment.

trades.thesis: Small-cap direct seller trading at -45% from its 1-year high despite explosive reported fundamentals: Q2 net sales doubled YoY to $69.7M (H1 $110.4M vs $57.4M), operating income doubled to $12.3M at ~80% gross margin, H1 operating cash flow of $39.5M built cash to $74.4M on a debt-free balance sheet. At ~$7.69 the equity appears deeply undervalued relative to run-rate earnings and net cash, with shareholder-friendly capital returns ($6.1M buybacks, dividends, new $15M authorization). A concrete catalyst exists: the June 2015 funding of a CNY 20M mandated deposit toward a mainland China direct selling license application, which could unlock the largest addressable market within the forecast window. Key discounts applied: (1) earnings/cash-flow quality is partly float-driven — deferred revenue ($8.2M), accrued commissions ($14.3M), and distributor eWallet balances inflate both revenue conversion and OCF, and commissions now consume >50% of sales; (2) extreme Hong Kong/China concentration with FX controls and direct-selling regulatory risk; (3) director/>5% holder Broady selling into company-funded buybacks and a full DTA valuation allowance. These justify sizing discipline but do not defeat the valuation-plus-momentum setup: the market has already de-rated the stock 45%, so much model/regulatory skepticism appears embedded in price while reported growth keeps accelerating.
trades.catalyst: China direct selling license application (CNY 20M deposit funded June 2015) plus continued quarterly beats; new $15M buyback authorization and dividend declared on filing date provide near-term support.
trades.invalidation: Q3 results showing decelerating revenue or commission ratio rising further above 50% of sales; any regulatory action or negative commentary on China/HK direct-selling model; loss of cash build or reversal of deferred revenue/eWallet float.

evidence_refs.why: Q2 net sales doubled YoY to $69.7M with operating income doubling to $12.3M at ~80% gross margin — explosive fundamental momentum that the market has not priced at a -45% drawdown.
$39.5M H1 operating cash flow vs $12.8M prior year, debt-free balance sheet with $74.4M cash against a small-cap market cap — extreme asset/income support limits downside.

Deferred revenue ($2.7M→$8.2M) and accrued commissions ($8.9M→$14.3M) build suggests forward demand signal, though part of OCF is non-recurring eWallet float — quality caveat that tempers but does not negate the growth claim.
Concrete dated regulatory milestone (license application deposit funded June 2015) provides a credible 90-180 day rerating mechanism for mainland expansion.

Majority of business via Hong Kong selling into China with explicit direct-selling prohibition risk, plus insider selling into company buybacks — key downside tail driver in an anti-pyramid-scheme sentiment environment.

trades.thesis: The Q2 2015 10-Q depicts a fundamentally sound mid-cap industrial (Aerospace + Industrial segments): operating income up 11.6% with margin expanding 14.1%->16.1%, gross margin +180bps, H1 operating cash flow $85.9M vs $64.9M, cash up to $82M, leverage 1.77x vs 3.25x covenant max, $377M undrawn revolver, no goodwill/trade-name impairment at the annual test, unqualified PwC opinion, and ordinary-course litigation only. However, the stock sits ~63% below its 1-year high, meaning the market is pricing something the filings only partially explain: reported net sales declined 2.2% YoY (FX cut ~$19.9M), management flags North American industrial and China softness, Aerospace tax holidays expire 2015-2016 raising the effective rate (already 28.8%), MRO faces deferred maintenance, and margin gains partly reflect easy prior-year comparisons ($3.9M purchase accounting + $4.4M restructuring charges in H1 2014). The only dated near-term catalyst is the small €50M Thermoplay bolt-on closing August 2015 — supportive but not a rerating mechanism. With no credible near-term catalyst to reverse a deep drawdown amid macro industrial softness and a rising tax rate, cheapness and quality are insufficient for a long candidate; fundamentals argue against shorting too, so this is a watch.
trades.catalyst: Thermoplay (€50M) closing in August 2015 plus continued Q3 margin delivery could stabilize sentiment, but neither is a forceful rerating event; no major catalyst (guidance raise, backlog inflection) is evidenced in filings before cutoff.
trades.invalidation: A Q3 print showing negative organic growth (FX no longer fully explaining the decline), further margin compression as tax holidays roll off, or goodwill impairment warning against the $583M goodwill balance would invalidate the thesis; also a break to new lows on the -63% drawdown chart would signal unresolved selling pressure.

evidence_refs.why: Q2 operating income +11.6% to $50.6M with margin 14.1%->16.1% shows genuine profitability momentum despite headline sales decline
H1 OCF of $85.9M vs $64.9M prior year and $82M cash balance support balance-sheet resilience and capital deployment
Leverage 1.77x vs 3.25x max and $377M undrawn revolver make financial distress scenarios remote, limiting downside tail
Signed July 20, 2015 bolt-on closing August 2015 is the only concrete near-term event, but at €50M it is too small to drive a rerating alone
Management-flagged softness in North American industrial and China removes a demand-driven rerating trigger over the forecast window
Expiring Aerospace tax holidays create a known earnings headwind through 2016 that caps multiple expansion
Reported sales fell 2.2% YoY; organic growth is masked by FX, so the market lacks a clean positive revenue print to rally on

trades.thesis: Nathan's Famous enters the window with genuinely healthy operations — Q1 FY2016 revenue +11% to $30.65M, Branded Products +15.6%, royalties +17%, operating income +12.3% to $7.6M, and operating cash flow doubled to $6.6M — but the equity story is dominated by the March 2015 leveraged dividend recap: $135M of 10.000% senior secured notes due 2020 funding a ~$116M special dividend, leaving a $(62.7)M stockholders' deficit, ~$13.5M/yr fixed interest against a seasonally peak-weighted earnings base, and indenture restrictions on future payouts. The stock sits 43% below its 1-year high at $25.28 with only ~$1.6M/day dollar volume, so any de-rating pressure meets thin marginal liquidity. There is no credible near-term rerating mechanism: the buyback authorization is nearly exhausted (115,285 shares left), no redemption wall or contract catalyst lands inside 90 days, and the residual dividend payments (~$250K) and option vesting are immaterial. Offsetting risks are live and dated: the NYS fast-food minimum wage push and the NLRB joint-employer ruling threaten franchise economics, a NYS tax review (2011–2014) is open, and franchise unit count is shrinking (291 vs 311). Cheapness on EV/operating income is real but is the classic value trap setup — a leveraged, illiquid micro-cap with negative equity and no catalyst. Base-rate skepticism and the absence of a rerating mechanism argue against a long; the solid cash generation ($51.6M cash + $7.8M securities vs $15.6M current liabilities) argues against an outright reject.
trades.catalyst: No dated near-term catalyst identified. Potential (unconfirmed) rerating paths: continued buyback-driven per-share compounding, a new repurchase authorization, or resolution of the NY minimum wage/NLRB overhang; next hard date is the Sept 15, 2017 Notes put/call, well beyond the 90-day window.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would flip to long-candidate if the company announced a new repurchase authorization, deleveraging/notes redemption plan, or if the stock de-rated further to a level where EV/FCF (post-interest) offered a wide margin of safety; it would flip to reject on evidence of Branded Products deceleration, covenant pressure, or adverse NYS minimum wage/NLRB outcomes materially compressing franchise economics.

evidence_refs.why: Revenue +11% to $30.65M with Branded Products +15.6% and royalties +17% shows the underlying franchise/licensing engine is intact — the core bull case if a rerating ever occurs.
New $3.7M quarterly interest expense cut net income ~43% YoY; headline earnings trend is negative and the market may continue to discount the leveraged profile.

$135M of 10% senior secured notes funding a $116M special dividend flipped equity to -$62.7M — an extractive recapitalization that raises the cost of capital and constrains flexibility; primary reason cheapness alone is insufficient.

$51.6M cash + $7.8M securities vs $15.6M current liabilities and doubled operating cash flow ($6.6M) makes near-term default/refinancing stress unlikely within 90 days — caps the tail but doesn't create upside.
Buyback continues but only 115,285 shares remain authorized and no new authorization or dated catalyst is disclosed — no credible near-term rerating mechanism.

trades.thesis: Methode Electronics presents a classic value trap vs. contrarian setup at the 2015-09-03 cutoff: shares are down ~43% from their 1-year high (~$22.01) yet Q1 FY2016 showed record profitability — gross margin expanded to 26.4% from 23.2%, net income rose 9.8% to $23.5M, and the balance sheet is clean ($167.9M cash, only $2.0M drawn on a $100M revolver, covenant compliance, positive ~$13.1M quarterly FCF). However, the bull case is undermined by three grounded negatives: (1) net sales fell 6.8% YoY with the Interface segment's operating income collapsing from $7.0M to $0.7M, meaning margin gains are concentrated, not broad-based; (2) operating cash flow fell $14.2M YoY on working-capital outflows, questioning earnings quality; and (3) virtually all of the $167.9M cash is held offshore and permanently reinvested, so the apparent net-cash cushion is not deployable domestically. Critically, specialist extraction found no dated, funded catalysts within 90 days — the Fuchs litigation ruling is an undated binary with counterclaims outstanding, and heavy reliance on two automotive customers (declining Ford Center Console volumes, FX headwinds of -$6.1M) leaves the top-line trajectory uncertain. Cheapness plus clean balance sheet gives tolerable downside, but without a confirmed near-term rerating mechanism this does not meet the long-candidate bar; it merits monitoring into the fiscal Q2 print.
trades.catalyst: Fiscal Q2 FY2016 earnings report (expected early October 2015): if gross margin holds near 26% on the Egypt ramp despite lower Ford volumes, the depressed post-drawdown multiple could re-rate; secondary binary event is the fully briefed Fuchs motions-to-dismiss ruling.
trades.invalidation: A Q2 print showing renewed Ford Center Console volume declines, gross-margin give-back below ~24%, further Interface segment profit erosion (already $7.0M -> $0.7M), or an adverse Fuchs ruling would invalidate the rerating setup and confirm structural decline.

evidence_refs.why: Q1 FY2016 net sales fell 6.8% YoY to $203.3M — top-line contraction caps any rerating thesis and argues against a long now.
Gross margin expanded to 26.4% from 23.2% with net income up 9.8% to $23.5M — record profitability at a deeply drawn-down price supports optionality if sustained.
Egypt low-cost manufacturing ramp is the identified structural driver of margin gains — the most plausible fundamental support for a future rerating.
High dependence on two large automotive customers (declining Ford Center Console volumes) is the key downside risk to both earnings and the multiple.
$167.9M cash is virtually all offshore/permanently reinvested — headline cash cannot fund domestic returns, discounting the apparent net-cash value support.
OCF fell $14.2M YoY to $19.0M on working-capital swings — quality-of-earnings caution that tempers the reported EPS growth.
Fully briefed motions-to-dismiss awaiting ruling — an undated binary legal overhang rather than a positive catalyst.

trades.thesis: Modine enters the window down ~43% from its 1-year high after a Q2 FY2016 print that was optically terrible ($32.1M operating loss, net sales -11%) but substantially distorted by a one-time $39.2M non-cash pension settlement charge. Stripping that out, the underlying picture is still clearly negative: six-month sales -12%, gross margin down 110-130 bps, FX headwinds ($74.9M YTD), weak off-highway/commercial vehicle volumes, and Brazil deterioration. The bull case rests on cheapness after the drawdown plus announced positives ($50M buyback authorization, new strategic framework, Airedale rebuild completion in H2 FY16 backed by $85.6M insurance proceeds). But the buyback is untested — zero open-market shares were repurchased in Q2 — there is no valuation evidence supplied, no guidance/backlog data, and the fundamental momentum is still pointing down. With no credible near-term rerating mechanism and decelerating fundamentals, this fails the long-candidate bar; liquidity ($64.9M cash + $211M revolver, covenant compliance) keeps bankruptcy-type tail risk contained, so the appropriate stance is watch rather than reject outright.
trades.catalyst: No dated, high-conviction rerating event within the window. The nearest candidates are completion of the Airedale Rawdon reconstruction in H2 FY2016 and any visible execution of the October 2015 $50M buyback / 'Strengthen, Diversify & Grow' framework — both real but unproven and unlikely to overcome FX and demand headwinds within 90 days.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would flip to long candidate if: (1) open-market buyback execution appears in subsequent filings, (2) FX stabilizes and organic sales inflect positive, or (3) gross margin recovers toward prior-year levels on completed restructuring savings; it would harden to reject if covenant headroom narrows or off-highway/Brazil volumes deteriorate further.

evidence_refs.why: -11% YoY sales with only ~$34.7M of the $43.3M decline from FX implies genuine volume weakness in off-highway/commercial vehicle end markets
$39.2M non-cash charge means headline operating loss overstates deterioration, but even ex-item operations are negative — limits both bearish overshoot and bullish re-rating case
Zero open-market repurchases in Q2 despite the new authorization; capital-return signal is untested and cannot be treated as a near-term catalyst
$64.9M cash plus $211M undrawn lines against ~$150.7M debt with covenant compliance affirmed makes balance-sheet/liquidity tail risk tolerable
+190 bps Americas gross margin from McHenry closure savings shows cost actions are working at segment level — a seed of a future thesis, not a current one

trades.thesis: Corcept shows a genuine commercial inflection: Korlym net product revenue roughly doubled YoY (Q3 $13.261M vs $7.282M; nine months $35.319M vs $17.537M), producing the first positive quarterly operating income ($102K vs $(5.103)M) and cutting nine-month operating cash burn to $(1.033)M from $(25.973)M. With $36.45M cash after $19.7M of warrant/option exercise proceeds and management guiding to cash-flow breakeven without new raises, the balance sheet supports the story near-term. The stock trades ~42% below its 1-year high (~$4.18), so the market has not yet credited the profitability inflection; dated catalysts inside the 90-day window (TNBC Phase 1/2 efficacy data by end-2015, CORT125134 Phase 2 starts in Q1 2016) provide a credible rerating mechanism beyond mere cheapness. Offsets are real but manageable within the horizon: the uncapped-from-2016 Biopharma royalty obligation (~$29.9M remaining, change-of-control acceleration to $45.0M with IP collateral), single-source manufacturing, method-of-use-only patents, and non-GAAP presentation that excludes SBC and accretion. Net: fundamental inflection + near-term catalysts + de-risked liquidity against a washed-out price gives an asymmetric setup, tempered by small-cap beta and binary pipeline risk.
trades.catalyst: Initial triple-negative breast cancer Phase 1/2 efficacy readout by end of 2015 and CORT125134 Phase 2 trial starts in both Cushing's and oncology in Q1 2016, both landing inside the 90-day window; secondary: Q4/full-year 2015 results confirming sustained profitability and cash-flow breakeven.
trades.invalidation: Q4 2015 revenue growth deceleration or receivables/rebate deterioration suggesting channel stuffing or gross-to-net erosion; a disappointing TNBC efficacy readout; any new equity raise at depressed prices contradicting the breakeven claim; covenant breach triggering the punitive 50%-of-sales royalty step-up.

evidence_refs.why: Korlym net product revenue +82% YoY in Q3 ($13.261M vs $7.282M) is the core rerating engine — a commercial-stage asset scaling rapidly, not just a story stock.
First positive quarterly operating income ($102K vs $(5.103)M loss YoY) with flat opex demonstrates operating leverage that supports a re-rating off trough valuation.
$19.7M of option/warrant proceeds lifting cash to $36.45M while operating burn fell to $(1.033)M for nine months materially reduces near-term financing/dilution risk — key to tolerable downside.
Dated Q1 2016 Phase 2 start for CORT125134 (plus year-end 2015 TNBC efficacy data per filing narrative) provides identifiable near-term news flow inside the forecast window.
Biopharma obligation accelerates up to $45.0M on change of control with IP as collateral — a structural overhang capping upside and a genuine tail risk.
Method-of-use-only patents on mifepristone limit moat durability; cheapness plus growth without IP protection would not justify a long.

trades.thesis: MiMedx reports genuinely strong Q3 2015 fundamentals — net sales +46% YoY to $49.0M (9M: $135.5M vs $78.7M), nine-month operating income $16.6M vs $2.4M, positive operating cash flow ($14.5M), ~90% gross margins, and a fortress balance sheet ($41.1M cash + $6.5M CDs, no debt, new $50M revolver). The stock sits ~42% below its 1-year high at $7.50, so much negativity appears priced. However, this fails the two-gate long test: (a) no credible near-term rerating mechanism — the filing discloses no hard-dated catalysts (CollaFix explicitly uncommercialized; FDA approval triggers only a $200K payment); and (b) downside is not clearly tolerable — AR nearly doubled to $46.8M (+75%, outpacing revenue) with a $20.1M working-capital drag that, combined with judgment-based hospital-consignment revenue recognition, raises channel-stuffing/revenue-quality risk; a consolidated securities class action (361 HCT/P misclassification) is in discovery with class certification pending; and FDA draft guidance explicitly contemplates that micronized products (~14% of 2014 revenue) may require a license or even recall. Heavy SBC ($12.6M 9M add-back; $17.7M unrecognized restricted stock) and a 14.6M-option overhang ($88.3M intrinsic value) dilute the equity story. Cheapness-plus-momentum without a dated catalyst earns a watch, not a long.
trades.catalyst: No hard-dated event disclosed in the filing. Nearest plausible rerating mechanisms: (1) year-end 2015 items flagged in the 10-Q — potential release of the full deferred-tax valuation allowance ("may release all or a portion of this valuation allowance by the end of 2015") boosting reported EPS, and Q4 earnings in early 2016 confirming sustained ~45%+ growth; (2) continued execution of the newly enlarged $50M buyback providing a persistent bid at a -42% drawdown; (3) resolution of the pending class-certification motion removing legal overhang. None is confirmed-dated within 90 days.
trades.invalidation: Watch converts to reject if: Q4/full-year results show decelerating revenue growth or further AR/DSO deterioration suggesting channel stuffing; FDA finalizes guidance restricting or forcing recall of micronized products; class action is certified or expands; or insider selling offsets the buyback bid. Conversely, a clean Q4 print with AR normalization plus valuation-allowance release would upgrade to long_candidate.

evidence_refs.why: Q3 net sales $49.0M (+46% YoY) and nine-month operating income $16.6M vs $2.4M — genuine operating momentum and leverage supporting a rerating case.

AR nearly doubled to $46.8M (+75%) vs year-end, consuming $20.1M of operating cash flow — quality-of-revenue red flag (consignment/distributor recognition) that caps conviction despite headline growth.

FDA draft guidance asserts micronized amniotic tissue is more than minimally manipulated with explicit recall-risk language; ~14% of 2014 revenue exposed — an unquantifiable binary overhang within the forecast window.

Securities fraud class action tied to 361 HCT/P classification in discovery with class certification motion pending since March 2015 — tail risk that management's 'no material impact' assertion does not credibly extinguish.
Board raised repurchase authorization to $50M in Oct 2015 (only $3.4M remained at 9/30) — management conviction signal and a mechanical demand source at depressed prices.
$41.1M cash + $6.5M CDs, no debt, new $50M undrawn revolver — downside is funding-constrained-free; distress scenario effectively ruled out.

trades.thesis: Green Brick (GRBK) screens optically cheap after a ~44% drawdown to $8.15, below its July 2015 $10.00 equity offering price, and the balance sheet was genuinely de-risked ($150M Greenlight term loan repaid with ~$170M net proceeds; debt/capitalization <7%). But the fundamental trajectory argues against a near-term rerating: Q3 revenue grew 51% yet nine-month operating profit declined YoY, residential gross margin compressed from ~32% to ~20%, attributable net income fell ($2.8M vs $3.7M in Q3) with EPS collapsing to $0.06 on ~56% share dilution, ~42% of consolidated income leaks to noncontrolling interests, and nine-month operating cash flow was negative (-$21.5M) amid an aggressive land/inventory build. Disclosure controls were deemed ineffective with unremediated material weaknesses, adding a quality/governance discount (Greenlight ~49.9% voting power, CEO's son running a consolidated subsidiary). The deleveraging catalyst is already behind the stock and failed to hold the price above the offering level; no dated forward catalyst exists in the filings. Cheapness plus a clean balance sheet is not sufficient without a credible rerating mechanism, so this is a watch rather than a long candidate.
trades.catalyst: None dated or imminent in filings. Potential future rerating triggers would be sequential gross-margin stabilization in upcoming quarters, remediation of material weaknesses, or deployment of the raised equity into accretive land deals — none verifiable within the 90-day window.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would turn constructive on demonstrated residential gross-margin recovery toward prior-year levels, positive operating cash flow as inventory monetizes, and concrete remediation of the material weaknesses; it turns outright bearish if Q4 margins compress further alongside continued inventory build.

evidence_refs.why: Residential gross margin fell from ~32% to ~20% YoY while revenue grew 73% — growth is being bought with margin give-up, undermining the core bull case for operating leverage.

~56% share count increase (31.3M to 48.8M) via the July 2015 $10.00 offering; per-share economics reset lower and the stock now trades below the institutional deal price with no re-rating mechanism visible.
~42% of consolidated nine-month net income accrues to noncontrolling interests, so headline growth overstates what accrues to common holders.
$150M high-cost Greenlight term loan extinguished and liens released; debt/capitalization <7% makes the downside scenario survivable even if margins stay weak.
Greenlight's ~49.9% voting stake aligns the dominant holder with a recovery above its $10 offering price, but also embeds related-party complexity and governance discount.
Clean legal posture removes one tail risk, though it does not offset unremediated control weaknesses noted in the accounting specialist's summary.

trades.thesis: Darling Ingredients trades at $10.00, ~48% below its 1-year high, after a Q3 FY2015 print showing a $(9.1)M net loss attributable, ~13% sales decline, widening DGD equity-method losses ($(12.0)M), and heavy FX translation losses ($131.8M YTD into AOCI of $(306)M). Much of this weakness is non-cash or macro-driven (FX, finished-product prices), while the underlying cash engine improved: nine-month OCF of $296.7M vs $179.3M, debt reduced to ~$2.02B, interest expense down to $82.2M from $110.8M, covenant compliance affirmed, and $920M revolver availability. Critically, there is a dated, filing-grounded rerating mechanism inside the window: the EPA committed to finalize 2014/2015 RFS volume requirements by November 30, 2015 — a direct read-through to the DGD JV that has been the main earnings drag. With the stock deeply de-rated, a $100M buyback authorized (~$94.1M remaining), and FCF positive (~$134M nine months), the setup offers credible upside optionality against a tolerable downside supported by cash flow and laddered maturities (2018/2021/2022). This is not cheapness alone — it is deep drawdown + dated regulatory catalyst + intact cash generation. Conviction is tempered by deteriorating GAAP operations, a reasonably possible Q4 Canada Fuel impairment, red-zone multiemployer pension exposure, and ~$2B debt against only $148.9M cash, so position as a modest-sized candidate rather than high-conviction.
trades.catalyst: EPA finalization of 2014/2015 RFS volume requirements by November 30, 2015 (within the forecast window), a direct earnings lever for the DGD renewable diesel JV that has been swinging to losses; secondary support from continued buyback execution under the $100M authorization.
trades.invalidation: A disappointing RFS final rule (volumes at or below proposal), a large Q4 Canada Fuel impairment beyond the flagged ~$30.1M goodwill, renewed commodity/FX deterioration pushing Adjusted EBITDA materially below the ~$106M quarterly run-rate, or any covenant stress signal would invalidate the thesis.

evidence_refs.why: Only dated, quote-grounded near-term catalyst across all extractions: EPA to finalize RFS volumes by Nov 30, 2015 — directly affects DGD JV economics and provides a concrete rerating mechanism inside the 90-day window.
Nine-month operating cash flow rose to $296.7M from $179.3M despite GAAP losses — cash generation funds deleveraging and limits balance-sheet downside while the equity is depressed.
Q3 net sales fell ~13% YoY with operating income down to $38.8M from $49.9M — confirms genuine fundamental deterioration that caps conviction and argues for modest sizing.
$100M board buyback (~$94.1M remaining through Aug 2017) with early execution signals management willingness to support the stock near these levels.
$148.9M cash plus $920.1M revolver availability against laddered maturities (TLA 2018, TLB 2021, notes 2022) makes forced-dilution/refinancing risk remote over 90 days.
Equity-method losses widened to $(12.0)M and investment balance shrank — the DGD drag is the key swing factor the RFS catalyst could reverse, framing the asymmetry.

trades.thesis: IDT trades at ~$7.09 (~$165M market cap) against $152.8M of cash+marketable securities, though roughly $93.5M of that is restricted or effectively unavailable, leaving meaningful but not full asset coverage. The stock is down ~47% from its 1-year high on a shrinking core: Q1 FY16 revenue fell 5.4% YoY to $390.6M and headline operating income collapsed (prior year inflated by the one-time $75.1M Fabrix gain), while underlying margins are thin (~1.2% net) despite cost-driven TPS operating income improvement and positive ~$14M quarterly operating cash flow. The credible rerating mechanism is the Board-approved three-way reorganization with the Zedge spin-off targeted for Q2 CY2016 — but that target lands at or beyond the edge of the 90-day window, remains subject to final Board/third-party approvals, and no record date or distribution ratio exists yet. Cheapness plus a hard-asset floor argues against severe downside, but there is no confirmed near-term catalyst certain to land within 90 days, and secular telecom decline plus a rising doubtful-accounts provision ($873K vs $44K YoY) offset the value case. This is a watch: the setup has a plausible sum-of-parts unlock, but timing risk and dual-class insider control mean I need confirmation of spin-off progress (record date, Form 10 effectiveness) before committing capital.
trades.catalyst: Zedge spin-off completion targeted for Q2 CY2016 (record date/ratio announcements would be the near-term trigger), plus Fabrix escrow release in April 2016 and Boss Revolution app v2 launch in Q2 CY2016; any of these landing inside the 90-day window would support a sum-of-parts rerating.
trades.invalidation: Delay or abandonment of the Zedge spin-off timetable, acceleration of Telecom Platform revenue decline beyond -5% YoY, further deterioration in receivables quality (doubtful-account provisions already up ~20x YoY), or continued post-spin drift lower would invalidate the thesis.

evidence_refs.why: $152.8M cash+securities vs ~$165M market cap anchors downside, though ~$93.5M is restricted/unavailable
Board-approved three-way split with Zedge spin targeted Q2 CY2016 is the only dated rerating mechanism, but sits at/outside the 90-day horizon and remains approval-contingent
-5.4% YoY revenue decline confirms secular erosion of the core telecom business, capping multiple expansion absent the spin
OCF improved to $14.0M from $8.3M on cost cuts — thin but positive cash generation supports dividend and runway
$25M undrawn revolver, zero drawn debt after mortgage repayment — no balance-sheet stress vector over 90 days
21.75M Class B vs 1.57M Class A implies concentrated insider control; minority holders depend entirely on management executing the announced reorganization

trades.thesis: Royal Gold enters Feb 2016 down ~55% from its 1-year high with an operating inflection that the market has not yet paid for: Q2 FY16 revenue grew ~60% YoY to $98.1M and operating income swung to +$27.2M as newly acquired streams (Pueblo Viejo silver effective Jan 1, 2016, Golden Star, Andacollo) began delivering. The six-month net loss is optical — driven by a one-time ~$64M tax charge on the Andacollo termination, not operations. Liquidity is adequate ($442.3M total including $300M undrawn revolver; covenants affirmed), covering dated commitments ($70M Golden Star payments, possible $75M Rainy River trigger). The rerating mechanism is credible: contractual stream ramps give visible sequential GEO/revenue growth into the May-quarter report, and the stock is levered to any stabilization in gold after a severe drawdown. Risks are real — debt doubled to $677.5M, ~90% gold revenue sensitivity, four-asset concentration (~65% of FY15 revenue), and Thompson Creek's distress threatening Mount Milligan — but they argue for sizing discipline rather than rejection. Cheapness alone is insufficient here; what earns the long candidacy is the dated delivery ramp plus depressed valuation.
trades.catalyst: Pueblo Viejo silver stream deliveries began Jan 1, 2016 and Golden Star Wassa underground production expected mid-2016 (stream stepping to 10.5%), driving sequential revenue/GEO growth into Q3 FY16 reporting (~May 2016); any stabilization or rebound in gold from the $1,106/oz quarter average would flow through at near-pure margin given the royalty cost structure.
trades.invalidation: Renewed gold-price breakdown below quarter-average levels (~$1,050-1,100/oz) compressing stream margins and reviving impairment risk on the ~$860M development/exploration-stage carrying value (incl. $380.7M Pascua-Lama); evidence of covenant stress or a dividend cut; material adverse development at Mount Milligan operator Thompson Creek.

evidence_refs.why: Q2 FY16 revenue +60% YoY to $98.1M with operating income swinging to +$27.2M — a credible operating inflection as newly acquired streams begin delivering, supporting a rerating mechanism rather than mere cheapness.

$442.3M total liquidity ($117.6M cash + $300M undrawn revolver) with affirmed covenant compliance makes the post-deployment balance sheet survivable through the 90-day window despite the sharp cash decline.
New streams (Pueblo Viejo silver from Jan 1, 2016; Golden Star; Andacollo) provide dated, contractually defined delivery ramp — a concrete near-term earnings driver within the forecast horizon.

The six-month $(31.0)M net loss is driven by a one-time $63.9M tax charge (194.3% effective rate) on the Andacollo termination, not operations — headline loss likely depresses sentiment without reflecting run-rate economics.
Thompson Creek's distress threatens the Mount Milligan stream, one of the largest revenue contributors — a genuine tail risk that caps conviction and position sizing.
~65% of FY2015 revenue from four properties plus ~90% gold sensitivity means a renewed gold drawdown would hit both cash flows and the multiple — key downside scenario.

trades.thesis: Malibu Boats at $12.78 (down ~47% from its 1-year high) pairs genuinely strong operating momentum with a credible near-term rerating mechanism. Q2 FY16 net sales +9% ($60.5M), six-month operating income +58% ($16.3M) on gross margin expansion and G&A discipline, and a swing to +$13.6M operating cash flow (vs -$4.4M) demonstrate the business is executing well despite the stock's de-rating. The $15M buyback authorized Feb 1, 2016 — funded from cash on hand against a $14.9M cash balance — is a concrete, dated catalyst that directly supports the share price into the seasonally strong spring selling season and the May fiscal Q3 print. Valuation is undemanding for the growth rate (annualized H1 net income ~$17M against a market cap in the mid-$200Ms, roughly mid-teens P/E). The bear case is real but mostly structural and known: a $96.6M TRA liability against a stockholders' deficit, ~10x higher interest expense from the 2015 term loan, an $11.7M immaterial NCI error correction, decelerating domestic retail demand, and a MY2016 warranty extension. These overhangs explain the discount but are largely priced in at a 47% drawdown; the first TRA payment (~$3M) is manageable and removes uncertainty. Cheapness alone would not qualify this, but cheapness plus a dated buyback catalyst plus accelerating operating leverage does.
trades.catalyst: Execution of the newly authorized $15M buyback (Feb 1, 2016) into a stock already down ~47% from its 1-year high, followed by fiscal Q3 FY16 results (May 2016) covering the seasonally strongest spring selling quarter; first TRA payment (~$3M) settling in April/May removes a known overhang rather than creating a surprise.
trades.invalidation: Fiscal Q3 FY16 results (due ~May 2016) showing flat-to-down net sales, gross margin compression, or further inventory build would confirm the demand-deceleration risk and invalidate the rerating thesis; failure to commence buyback execution by late Q2 2016, or any covenant amendment/waiver, would also be disqualifying.

evidence_refs.why: Buyback authorization ($15M, Feb 1, 2016) plus management's 12-month liquidity sufficiency assertion gives a concrete, near-term share-retirement mechanism at depressed prices; cash of $14.9M and +$13.6M H1 OCF fund it without stressing covenants.
Six-month operating income +58% YoY with gross margin expansion and G&A decline demonstrates genuine operating leverage — the fundamental engine for a rerating, not just a cheap multiple.
OCF swing to +$13.6M from -$4.4M validates earnings quality and funds debt amortization and the TRA payment without refinancing risk.

$96.6M TRA payable against a stockholders' deficit is the principal bear case: it caps upside attribution to common holders and creates recurring cash outflows; it is why this is a candidate, not a conviction position.
Management's own flag of decelerating domestic retail demand growth is the key fundamental risk to the rerating thesis; a weak spring selling season would invalidate it.
$11.7M NCI error correction is an accounting-quality flag; immaterial per the filing, but it raises the evidentiary bar and justifies position-size restraint.

trades.thesis: Zillow Group enters the window down ~51% from its 1-year high ($19.18 close 2016-02-11) despite grounded fundamentals that are far stronger than the price action implies: FY2015 revenue nearly doubled to $644.7M (+98%, Trulia-aided), Adjusted EBITDA grew to $87.6M, and liquidity is ample ($523.3M cash/investments and $493.7M working capital against only $230M of 2.75% convertible notes due 2020). The Trulia integration restructuring (~350 headcount reduction) and Market Leader divestiture are complete, so the heaviest one-time costs are behind. The disclosed spring/summer seasonal peak in home sales supports Premier Agent ad spend into Q2, and the first clean post-integration quarterly print is the natural rerating trigger within the 90-day window. The bear case is real but mostly non-cash or backward-looking: the $(148.9)M GAAP loss is dominated by $105-120M of share-based comp and $63M amortization, while operating cash flow of $22.7M remains positive. This is a beaten-down, liquid ($16.7M ADV), still-growing franchise where sentiment — not solvency — drove the derating; cheapness alone would not qualify it, but the combination of deep drawdown, intact demand metrics (123.7M average monthly unique users, +61% YoY), completed restructuring, and a seasonal/catalyst path to a positive print makes it a sized-long candidate with defined invalidation.
trades.catalyst: Q1 2016 earnings report (expected early May 2016, within the 90-day window) as the first clean post-integration quarter, showing whether revenue momentum (+98% FY2015, 123.7M monthly unique users +61% YoY) converts into narrowing losses and stable Agent Advertiser counts during the seasonally strongest spring/summer home-selling period; secondary: resolution or favorable development in the June 2016 trade secrets trial removing the legal overhang.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q1 2016 results show sequential Agent Advertiser declines accelerating (92,366 in Q4 2015 was already down from 103,415 in Q1), revenue guidance implying organic deceleration post-Market Leader divestiture, further OCF deterioration below ~$20M/quarter, or adverse developments in the June 2016 trade secrets trial; a sustained break below the pre-cutoff low on volume would also invalidate the oversold-rerating setup.

evidence_refs.why: Grounded +98% revenue growth to $644.7M establishes demand-side momentum that can support a rerating once integration costs roll off.
$523.3M cash/investments vs $230M 2.75% 2020 Notes gives a multi-year runway, capping near-term solvency/dilution risk and making the 51% drawdown survivable.

Widened $(148.9)M net loss and halved operating cash flow ($22.7M) are the key quality caveats; they cap conviction and argue for position sizing discipline rather than rejection given heavy non-cash SBC ($105-120M).
~350-employee restructuring tied to the $2.0B Trulia deal is largely executed, providing a plausible mechanism for margin improvement into 2016 quarters.
Disclosed spring/summer seasonal peak in home sales aligns the 90-day window with Zillow's strongest advertising-demand quarters — a grounded, recurring rerating tailwind.
Dual-class structure and blank-check preferred entrench insiders and dilute Class A economics without recourse — a persistent discount factor arguing against a high-conviction oversized position.
Completed divestiture simplifies the story but removes revenue and confirms a $4.4M loss; reduces both upside optionality and downside complexity.

trades.thesis: Ryder enters the window deeply washed out (-46.5% from its 1-year high, ~$38 vs ~$99 peak) after a broad early-2016 industrial/energy-driven derating, yet FY2015 fundamentals were solid: pre-tax earnings from continuing ops +39% to $469M on 6% operating revenue growth, $1.44B operating cash flow, and a clean PwC ICFR opinion. The credible rerating mechanism is a funded, dated FCF inflection — management guides ~+$100M 2016 free cash flow versus -$728M in 2015 as growth capex declines — plus $22M annualized cost savings substantially complete by end-Q1 2016 and PATH Act bonus depreciation reducing federal tax payments. The stock appears to price cyclical-trough residual values and distress-level leverage concerns (278% D/E) that the actual cash generation does not support. Key risks are real but identifiable: late-2015 used tractor market weakness with a 45% build in held-for-sale units, elevated customer/auto concentration in SCS, and a prior-period revision for sale-leaseback structures (stated immaterial). With the market already assigning severe downside, asymmetric payoff favors a long position sized against residual-value and refinancing tail risk.
trades.catalyst: Q1 2016 earnings (late April): completion of workforce reduction delivering $22M annualized savings, first print showing the guided swing from -$728M to ~+$100M free cash flow as fleet capex declines, and any stabilization commentary on used tractor pricing/residuals; secondary catalyst is execution of the $543M 2016 debt refinancing at post-February credit-spread normalization.
trades.invalidation: Used vehicle pricing deteriorates further rather than stabilizing (inventory liquidation at losses), Q1 2016 results show rental demand erosion or SCS weakness tied to auto production cuts, or the guided FCF inflection is walked back / refinancing of 2016 maturities executes at punitive spreads — any of which would signal the cycle is still worsening rather than bottoming.

evidence_refs.why: Guided ~$100M 2016 FCF vs -$728M in 2015 on lower growth/replacement capex — the clearest near-term rerating mechanism for a capital-intensive fleet business priced for distress.
$22M annualized savings substantially complete by end of Q1 2016 provides a funded, dated earnings catalyst within the forecast window.
Weakening used tractor market plus 45% inventory build is the primary fundamental risk; residual-value deterioration could undercut both disposal gains and the FCF inflection.
278% debt/equity and rising total debt ($5.5B) cap upside and make the thesis sensitive to funding costs and refinancing execution.
$1.44B operating cash flow from continuing operations confirms underlying cash generation is intact despite negative FCF from growth capex — supports tolerable downside.
Revision of 2012–2014 financials (sale-leaseback deconsolidation) is an accounting-quality flag warranting a discount, though characterized as immaterial with a clean PwC ICFR opinion.
Top-10 SCS customers = 54% of SCS revenue and ~41% auto-industry exposure add idiosyncratic revenue risk if auto production rolls over.

trades.thesis: Mercer International (NBSK market pulp; Rosenthal/Stendal/Celgar) screens as a leveraged cyclical at a visible trough: the stock is down ~60% from its 1-year high ($4.26 pre-cutoff close, ~$276M equity vs $650M high-yield notes), and FY2015 shows price-driven revenue erosion (-11.9% to $946.2M on flat volumes). Against that, the filing evidence supports trough economics rather than deterioration: consolidated cash production costs fell to $465/ADMT (from $535/$577), cash rose to $99.6M with current debt eliminated, PwC issued clean financials and ICFR opinions, and the board declared a $0.115 quarterly dividend on Feb 10, 2016 — a costly signal of cash-flow confidence made days before the cutoff. The rerating mechanism is cyclical mean-reversion in realized pulp prices amplified by operating leverage from lower unit costs, plus a dated idiosyncratic catalyst: the NAFTA arbitration decision expected sometime in 2016. Cheapness alone would be insufficient, but here cheapness coincides with improving unit costs, a strengthened liquidity position, a maintained dividend, and a pending legal catalyst — a credible near-term rerating setup. Risks are real: structural subordination of the notes, ~3.6M ADMT of announced hardwood capacity additions pressuring prices, tariff expiries (2019/2020/2024), ERP implementation control risk, and impairment exposure if markets weaken further. Net: modestly favorable asymmetry at a deeply depressed base, sized as a candidate rather than a high-conviction position given unresolved debt/covenant disclosure gaps.
trades.catalyst: NAFTA tribunal decision expected sometime in 2016 (unquantified recovery on Celgar energy treatment), plus the April 5, 2016 dividend payment as a near-term confidence marker; any stabilization/uptick in realized NBSK pricing after the 2015 decline would drive outsized EPS torque given flat volumes and falling unit costs.
