trades.thesis: Dollar General at ~$76 is down ~50% from its 1-year high, and the Q3 FY2024 10-Q (filed at the cutoff) confirms why: diluted EPS fell ~29% YoY ($0.89 vs $1.26), gross margin slipped 18 bps on markdowns/damages/consumables mix, SG&A deleveraged 111 bps including $32.7M hurricane costs with ~$10M more guided for Q4, and management explicitly states shrink will materially pressure fiscal 2024 results. The core customer is financially stressed (some relying on credit cards for basics), the promotional environment is intensifying, and new-store returns are being pressured by cost inflation. Capital returns are fully suspended (zero buybacks in FY2024 YTD, none planned in Q4, to preserve the investment-grade rating), removing a support mechanism, and an expanded-class securities class action (May 2020–Aug 2024) plus derivative suits carry an acknowledged potential material adverse effect. Offsets are real but insufficient for a 90-day long: +5.0% sales/+1.3% comps, ~$2.2B YTD operating cash flow funding capex, dividends, and $765M debt paydown with no CP outstanding. Critically, there is no credible near-term rerating mechanism — no funded catalyst, no buyback, no evidence of margin inflection (self-checkout shrink mitigation is only 'early trend'), and the next earnings print lands inside the window with risk of another negative guide. Deep drawdown plus solid cash generation argues against rejection, but cheapness alone does not satisfy the bar; this is a quality-of-earnings problem awaiting visible margin stabilization.
trades.catalyst: None funded within the 90-day window. Potential future rerating triggers (not yet in hand): stabilization of shrink/damages drag, easing promotional intensity, resolution or quantification of the securities class action, or resumption of buybacks once deleveraging targets are met.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would flip positive if Q4/FY24 results (due ~mid-March 2025) show sequential gross-margin stabilization, shrink improvement beyond self-checkout early trends, or management signaling buyback resumption; thesis would turn decisively negative on guidance cuts, covenant/ratings pressure, or material adverse litigation developments.

evidence_refs.why: Management explicitly guides that shrink will materially pressure fiscal 2024 full-year results, with damages continuing through year-end — the core unresolved earnings drag.
SG&A ratio up 111 bps YoY (hurricanes, labor, D&A) plus gross margin -18 bps shows broad-based operating deleverage, not a one-off.
Core low-income customers relying on credit cards for basics signals continued demand-quality deterioration and consumables mix headwind.
Zero buybacks all year and none planned in Q4 to protect the IG rating removes a key per-share support mechanism during the drawdown.
Company itself flags covenant compliance and downgrade risk; combined with litigation tail risk this bounds how much of the -50% drawdown is 'cheap' versus impaired.
+5.0% net sales and +1.3% comps show the top line is intact — the reason this stays on a watch list rather than being rejected outright.

trades.thesis: CRISPR Therapeutics enters the window deeply de-rated (-56% from 1-year high, ~$39.41 close vs prior ATM executions at ~$122.73) with a genuinely strong balance sheet: $1,903.8M in cash and marketable securities against roughly an $3.4B market cap (~85.77M shares), guided to fund operations for at least 24 months. That liquidity floor argues against bankruptcy-style tail risk and makes the stock cheap on enterprise-value terms. However, cheapness alone does not make a long candidate. The filing discloses no dated clinical or regulatory catalyst within the next 90-180 days, and a concrete negative inflection begins precisely in this window: the option to defer >$110.3M/year of CASGEVY costs expired starting 2025, with expenses expected to exceed the company's revenue share for the foreseeable future — raising burn and increasing the probability of dilution via the active $600M Jefferies ATM ($363.7M capacity remaining). Vertex controls the lead commercial program, limiting company-specific news flow, and Swiss anti-takeover provisions plus voting caps suppress M&A optionality. Net: tolerable downside but no credible near-term rerating mechanism grounded in the known filings; the setup favors patience over initiation.
trades.catalyst: No dated clinical/regulatory catalyst is present in the supplied filing excerpts within the 90-day window. Potential rerating mechanisms would be external to this filing — e.g., CASGEVY commercial uptake updates from Vertex, pipeline data readouts (CTX112/CTX131), or sector-wide biotech risk-appetite recovery — none of which are grounded in the known documents.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would flip positive on evidence of a dated near-term catalyst (clinical readout, regulatory milestone, or CASGEVY commercial traction disclosed by Vertex) or a shift toward non-dilutive funding; it would turn decisively negative if the company begins drawing down the remaining $363.7M ATM at prevailing prices (~$39), confirming value-destructive dilution, or if cash burn accelerates materially beyond plan after the CASGEVY deferral expiry.

evidence_refs.why: $1,903.8M cash/equivalents/marketable securities at YE2024 vs ~$3.4B market cap gives a low effective enterprise value and removes going-concern/near-term financing pressure as a downside driver.
Explicit ≥24-month runway guidance means no forced capital raise within the forecast horizon, supporting a 'watch' rather than 'reject' stance.
Loss of the >$110M/yr CASGEVY cost-deferral option beginning 2025 creates a concrete funded headwind and rising burn exactly during the 90-day window, undermining a near-term rerating thesis.
Explicit disclosure that substantial additional dilutive funding will be needed, corroborated by an active ATM with $363.7M remaining capacity, caps upside via overhang.
Active Jefferies ATM ($233.2M sold at avg $122.73, well above current price) signals management willingness to issue equity far above spot but also institutionalizes dilution mechanics.

trades.thesis: Biogen at $139.39 is deeply depressed (-43% from 1-year high) on a shrinking core: FY2024 total revenue -1.6% with the MS franchise down 6.7% (-$312.1M) on Interferon/TYSABRI competitive erosion, partially offset by rare disease launches (+10.3%; SKYCLARYS $382.5M, ZURZUVAE $72.2M, QALSODY $32.4M). The bull case rests on valuation support from ~$2.9B operating cash flow, ~$2.4B cash, and Fit for Growth cost cuts (-9.0% opex), but this is cheapness, not a rerating mechanism. Critically, the filings supply no dated near-term catalysts: no PDUFA/CHMP dates for felzartamab/nusinersen/salanersen in the excerpts, no FY2025 guidance beyond a quantified IRA Part D headwind ($50-100M concentrated in SKYCLARYS and MS), and — tellingly — zero share repurchases in 2023-2024 despite $2.1B of remaining authorization, signaling management itself does not treat the stock as compellingly cheap. EPS +40.3% is largely optical (lapping ~$393M of 2023 Reata equity-comp charges plus an $88.6M PRV gain), so reported earnings momentum will not carry the narrative. With the known 90-day window containing only the IRA headwind as a dated item and Q1 earnings likely to re-confirm both launch traction and legacy erosion, there is no credible mechanism to close a 43% drawdown gap within 90 days. Deep value with tolerable balance-sheet downside, but timing risk dominates; watch for launch trajectory inflection or capital-return activation before committing.
trades.catalyst: No dated regulatory/PDUFA catalysts disclosed within the 90-day window; nearest plausible rerating events are Q1 2025 results (~late April) showing whether SKYCLARYS/ZURZUVAE launch momentum absorbs the quantified IRA Part D headwind, or an unexpected initiation of buybacks under the idle $2.1B authorization. Absent either, the stock likely tracks sector beta.
trades.invalidation: Thesis upgrades to long candidate if: (a) management initiates meaningful buybacks against the $2.1B authorization, (b) SKYCLARYS quarterly trajectory clearly outruns the IRA drag, or (c) a dated regulatory catalyst for felzartamab/salanersen emerges. Downgrade to reject if Q1 prints show SKYCLARYS deceleration plus continued double-digit MS erosion.

evidence_refs.why: Core franchise erosion (-6.7%, -$312.1M) is the dominant bearish driver and remains unresolved entering 2025
SKYCLARYS/ZURZUVAE/QALSODY rare disease growth (+$185.1M, +10.3%) is the only credible rerating engine, but too small to offset MS decline yet
~$2.4B cash and ~$2.9B operating cash flow support a floor valuation and fund pipeline/milestones without dilution
$2.1B authorized but zero repurchases in two years removes a potential capital-return rerating mechanism
Quantified $50-100M 2025 headwind concentrated in SKYCLARYS/MS directly pressures the growth narrative that bulls rely on
Top-line contraction with EPS growth flattered by lapping one-time items signals weak underlying operating momentum

trades.thesis: Marathon Bancorp has one genuinely credible rerating mechanism — the second-step mutual-to-stock conversion Plan adopted December 10, 2024 — which historically compresses the MHC discount and attracts conversion-fund flows. The balance sheet is clean and de-risking (cash +54% to $16.2M, FHLB advances cut to $10M, narrowing AOCI loss, ~14.26% bank capital), limiting downside. However, the setup fails the near-term test: there is no announced timetable, exchange ratio, or offering size, so completion of regulatory approvals plus depositor and minority-stockholder votes within 90 days is speculative. Meanwhile core earnings are deteriorating sharply (Q2 net income $51K vs. $272K YoY on NIM compression and shrinking loans), removing any fundamental floor for appreciation while the catalyst idles. At -47.6% from its 1-year high, much of the conversion anticipation may already be unwound, but cheapness alone does not qualify this as a long candidate. Watch for appraisal/exchange-ratio disclosure or an announced offering timeline.
trades.catalyst: Second-step conversion milestones: independent appraisal setting offering size/price, regulatory approval, and depositor/minority stockholder votes; secondary support from the small REO litigation settlement recovery expected in the quarter ending March 31, 2025.
trades.invalidation: Conversion timeline slips beyond two quarters without appraisal/exchange-ratio disclosure or S-corporation/holding-company filings progressing, while quarterly net income remains near breakeven — at which point the equity re-rates down toward book-less-AOCI value.

evidence_refs.why: Second-step conversion Plan adopted Dec 10, 2024 with subscription/community offering is a dated structural event that historically rerates thrift equities, but no timetable or exchange ratio is disclosed, so it may not land inside 90 days.
Q2 FY25 net income fell to $51K from $272K YoY with NII compression and provision swing — weak fundamentals undercut the case for paying up now despite the pending catalyst.
Cash up 54.4% to $16.2M, FHLB advances cut to $10M, AOCI loss narrowing — de-risking balance sheet supports strong bank capital (~14.26%) and limits downside.
Small recovery expected in quarter ending March 31, 2025 provides a modest near-term earnings bump but is immaterial to valuation.
MHC owns 55% with insider control across all three entities; second-step conversion would eliminate this overhang, but until approved the discount persists.

trades.thesis: Agios (AGP, inferred from stem) trades at $32.81, down ~47% from its 1-year high, with ~$1.5B in cash/securities, no debt, and 57.3M shares outstanding — implying roughly $26/share of net cash against a ~$1.9B market cap, so the enterprise value assigned to PYRUKYND plus pipeline is small. However, the FY2024 'profitability' is entirely non-recurring (Vorasidenib royalty sale/milestone), operations remain deeply loss-making with accelerating burn (~$390M/yr), and the one clearly dated rerating catalyst — the thalassemia sNDA PDUFA on Sept 7, 2025 — falls well outside the 90-day window. Within the forecast horizon there is no confirmed binary event; the setup is a cash-floored option on a September approval, subject to sector beta, dilution risk (no committed external funding), and a bear-flag January 2025 USPI hepatotoxicity update that raises approval-risk questions. Cheapness relative to cash plus a real future catalyst earns a watch, not a long: the required near-term rerating mechanism inside 90 days is absent, and the cash floor is eroding at ~$100M/quarter while management explicitly flags capital raises.
trades.catalyst: PYRUKYND thalassemia sNDA PDUFA goal date September 7, 2025 (with potential AdComm/pre-approval momentum building in H2), plus EMA MAA review progress; both sit at or beyond the 90-day horizon, making them positioning anchors rather than in-window rerating events.
trades.invalidation: Negative FDA signals ahead of the PDUFA (AdComm scheduling, complete response letter, or safety-driven label expansion like the Jan 2025 hepatocellular injury USPI update), a large dilutive financing announced before the approval, or a break below the net-cash support level (~$26) signaling market disbelief in the asset's value.

~$1.5B cash/securities, no debt, 57.3M shares implies ~$26/share net cash vs $32.81 price — a partial valuation floor that limits downside tail.

Post-oncology-divestiture concentration in PYRUKYND makes the stock a single-franchise regulatory story — binary risk profile around thalassemia/SCD approvals.
EPO oppositions on two European PYRUKYND patents add moderate IP overhang, though non-primary patents limit severity.
No committed external funding and explicit dilution/capital-raise warnings; with ~$390M annual burn, equity issuance risk caps upside during the waiting period.

trades.thesis: Savers Value Village enters the window at $11.26, down ~46% from its 1-year high, but the freshly filed FY2024 10-K supplies no credible near-term rerating mechanism and several new negatives. The filing discloses a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting (with explicit restatement risk language), $761.3M of non-investment-grade debt ($716.8M after the Feb 6, 2025 $44.5M note redemption) with restrictive covenants that limit dividends and repurchases, and extreme Ares control (84.6% ownership, majority board designation, consent rights over major corporate actions) that caps any takeover/speculative premium. Capital-return support is minimal: only $18.1M remains on the buyback and debt terms constrain it; no dividends are anticipated. Operations add structural concerns — brick-and-mortar-only with no online channel, no long-term supply agreements with nonprofit partners, and CPC automation exclusivity expiring Dec 2025 after Australia rights lapsed Oct 2024. Critically, the supplied excerpts contain no income statement, cash flow, or comparable-store-sales data, so even the 'cheap after a 46% drawdown' case is unverified rather than demonstrated. Near-term liquidity is adequate ($123.8M undrawn revolver), so outright distress is not the base case, but with no earnings visibility, no funded catalysts before June's annual meeting, and an active accounting-quality overhang, the stock fails both prongs of the long-candidate test: no credible rerating mechanism and unquantified-but-real downside from restatement/covenant/leverage tail risks. Deep value traps in leveraged, controlled companies with fresh material weaknesses have poor 90-day base rates.
trades.catalyst: None credible within 90 days: only dated event is the June 4, 2025 annual meeting; CPC exclusivity expiry (Dec 2025) and buyback expiry (Nov 8, 2025) fall outside the horizon. A material-weakness remediation disclosure or Q1 print beating depressed expectations would be the only plausible rerating triggers, but neither is evidenced in the filings.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would be invalidated by: (1) rapid remediation of the ICFR material weakness with clean auditor attestation, (2) disclosed acceleration of the buyback or an Ares-sponsored capital return/take-private, or (3) FY2024/Q1 results showing deleveraging and stable sales-yield trends that support a de-risked equity story.

evidence_refs.why: Freshly disclosed material weakness in ICFR creates elevated misstatement/restatement risk; remediation status unverified — an active negative overhang, not a cleared one.

Ares owns 84.6% with board-designation and consent rights; controlled-company status plus registration rights create minority disenfranchisement and share-sale overhang, limiting any takeover/activism rerating path.

$761.3M total debt (reduced to $716.8M post-Feb 6 redemption) against a small equity base; non-investment grade, variable-rate exposure, and covenants that restrict repurchases/dividends cap equity upside.
$123.8M undrawn revolver and completed $44.5M note redemption show near-term liquidity is adequate — downside is not imminent distress, but leverage still constrains equity optionality.
No e-commerce channel and no long-term supply agreements with NPPs leave unit economics (sales yield) exposed without operational offsets visible in the excerpts.
Only $18.1M remains under the $50M authorization and debt terms limit repurchases — insufficient to serve as a price-support mechanism.

trades.thesis: ICON plc trades ~42% below its 1-year high ($201.84 vs prior peak), and the FY2024 20-F confirms a genuinely improving balance sheet: total debt down to $3,446M from $3,806M YoY, $4,568.6M of the term loan repaid since the PRA merger ($2,581.8M funded by cash flow), a fully undrawn $500M revolver, retained earnings growth to $2,724.8M, and a Moody's outlook revision to positive alongside S&P BBB-. However, the specialist extractions surface no dated near-term operating catalyst: no revenue/bookings/backlog figures, no guidance, and explicit company disclosures that backlog conversion may slow and that biotech client funding pressure could reduce demand and pricing. The drawdown itself implies the market is pricing a bookings/demand problem that the filing excerpts neither quantify nor refute. Deleveraging is a slow-burn support, not a 90-day rerating mechanism, and judgment-heavy percentage-of-completion revenue plus $8.1B goodwill/$4.9B intangibles from the PRA merger add impairment/estimate-revision tail risk if demand deteriorates further. Cheapness alone does not qualify this as a long candidate without evidence of a bookings inflection or credible near-term catalyst.
trades.catalyst: No dated near-term operating catalyst disclosed in the filings; the nearest identifiable event is the $500M 2026 Notes refinancing and potential Moody's upgrade to investment grade, both of which are capital-structure events unlikely to drive equity rerating within 90 days absent a bookings inflection.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would flip toward long_candidate if Q1 2025 results show book-to-bill back above 1.0x with stabilized cancellations and management guiding to reaccelerating net new business awards, or if biotech funding conditions visibly ease; it would harden toward reject on further guidance cuts or goodwill impairment signals against the $8.1B PRA-related goodwill balance.

evidence_refs.why: $4,568.6M term loan repaid since merger ($2,581.8M via cash flow) evidences genuine cash generation and balance-sheet repair, but is a multi-year trend already known to the market rather than a fresh rerating trigger.
Moody's positive outlook (Q4 2024) with S&P BBB- affirmed supports eventual cheaper refinancing of the 2026 notes; supportive but slow-acting.
Company's own risk disclosure that backlog conversion may slow directly undermines the demand visibility needed for a near-term multiple recovery.
Biotech client funding pressure is the sector-wide headwind most plausibly responsible for the -42% drawdown; nothing in the filings indicates it is abating within 90 days.

Judgment-heavy percentage-of-completion revenue with significant third-party accruals raises earnings-quality risk precisely when estimates are being cut; combined with missing income-statement/cash-flow detail in excerpts, limits conviction in any valuation floor.

trades.thesis: Sterling Infrastructure presents a favorable asymmetry after a -42% drawdown from its 1-year high despite fundamentally solid FY2024 results: revenue ~$2.12B with operating income rising to $264.6M (12.5% margin vs 10.4%), unqualified financials/ICFR opinions from Grant Thornton, no restatements or unresolved SEC comments, and a net cash balance sheet ($664.2M cash vs $317.2M drawn revolver debt). The headline backlog decline ($2.07B -> $1.69B) is largely mechanical — $491.3M removed via the RHB deconsolidation — implying organic backlog was roughly flat-to-up, a distinction the market may reprice once clarified. Reported earnings are flattered by a one-time $91.3M non-cash gain, so valuation must be assessed on normalized earnings, but even normalized profitability trends are improving. Key risks are real but mostly outside the 90-day window: the credit facility matures April 2, 2026 (~13 months out), lender-consent/cross-default provisions reduce flexibility, and ~$581M goodwill+intangibles carry qualitative-only testing. With deep drawdown, clean accounting, net cash, an active $200M buyback authorization, and a mechanical-looking backlog decline, the setup offers a credible rerating mechanism with tolerable downside — cheapness alone is not the argument; the argument is mispricing of the backlog optics against verifiable operating quality.
trades.catalyst: Q1 2025 earnings report (expected early May 2025) presenting organic backlog/bookings excluding RHB, likely clarifying that the headline backlog decline is deconsolidation-driven rather than demand-driven; continued E-Infrastructure (data-center) award momentum and heavy-highway margin progression could drive rerating from a deeply depressed multiple.
trades.invalidation: Q1 2025 results or disclosures showing negative organic book-to-bill excluding RHB, E-Infrastructure margin compression, covenant pressure or failed refinancing progress on the April 2026 facility, or further multiple compression in construction/infrastructure names would invalidate the rerating thesis.

evidence_refs.why: Unqualified opinions on financials and ICFR with 404(b) attestation support earnings credibility at a moment when the stock's -42% drawdown may reflect sentiment rather than fundamental deterioration.
$91.3M non-cash gain means reported FY2024 income overstates run-rate earnings; requires normalizing before assessing valuation, tempering but not negating the operating-momentum story.

Backlog decline to $1.69B is largely mechanical ($491.3M RHB removal); implied organic backlog (~$1.69B vs ~$1.58B ex-RHB prior year) actually grew — a potential positive-surprise narrative if the market has priced the headline decline.
$664.2M cash vs $317.2M drawn variable-rate debt indicates net cash position, making the April 2026 maturity a manageable refinancing task rather than a solvency risk within the 90-day horizon.
$200M repurchase authorization provides discretionary support into weakness after a 42% drawdown.
Termination-for-convenience across substantially all backlog plus bonding capacity constraints cap how much weight backlog carries in the thesis; supports moderate rather than aggressive sizing.

trades.thesis: Entrada Therapeutics (NGM, ~$12.02, -44% from 1y high) enters the window with an unusually dense, dated catalyst path for a clinical-stage biotech: the FDA lifted the ENTR-601-44 clinical hold on 2025-02-24, MHRA authorized ELEVATE-44-201 on 2025-02-03, and management states the UK trial initiation is on track for Q2 2025 — inside the 90-day horizon. This satisfies the near-term rerating requirement rather than mere cheapness. Downside is tolerable over the window because management asserts cash/marketable securities fund operations into Q2 2027, and the Vertex collaboration ($250M upfront+equity; VX-670 Phase 2 MAD ongoing since Nov 2024) supplies non-dilutive validation. However, base rates for pre-revenue biotech versus SPY are near coin-flip: the platform is self-described as unproven, only one Phase 1 has been completed, losses will increase substantially, a $150M ATM creates dilution/supply overhang, ~73% insider concentration and anti-takeover provisions limit re-rating channels, and much of the hold-lift news may already be priced into the Feb 26 close. Position as a modest, catalyst-anchored candidate sized for binary outcomes, not a high-conviction bet.
trades.catalyst: ELEVATE-44-201 UK trial initiation in Q2 2025 (within ~90 days of cutoff), following the Feb 24, 2025 FDA clinical hold lift on ENTR-601-44 and Feb 3, 2025 MHRA authorization.
trades.invalidation: Slippage or delay of ELEVATE-44-201 initiation past Q2 2025, any new regulatory/clinical hold, aggressive ATM issuance into weakness, or a broad biotech risk-off leg that drags small-cap clinical names regardless of idiosyncratic progress.

evidence_refs.why: FDA lifted the ENTR-601-44 clinical hold on 2025-02-24, three days before cutoff — a fresh, dated regulatory de-risking event that removes a known overhang and enables US trial progress.

Company states it is on track to initiate ELEVATE-44-201 in the UK in Q2 2025 — a concrete, quote-grounded pipeline milestone falling inside the 90-day forecast window, providing the required near-term rerating mechanism.

Management asserts cash, equivalents and marketable securities fund operations into Q2 2027 (~16 months beyond cutoff), making a financing-driven collapse within the 90-day horizon unlikely and keeping downside tolerable.

$250.0M received from Vertex ($223.7M upfront + $26.3M equity at $16.26/share) plus VX-670 Phase 2 MAD ongoing since Nov 2024 provides non-dilutive external validation and funded partnered development.
$150.0M ATM program creates an active dilution/supply overhang that caps upside and argues for conservative sizing despite the constructive setup.

No product revenue since inception, losses expected to increase substantially, and an admittedly unproven EEV platform mean valuation rests entirely on pipeline optionality — a structural risk limiting conviction.

trades.thesis: Crinetics (clinical-stage endocrine biotech) screens as a cash-protected lottery ticket rather than a clean long: ~$1.4B cash/investments vs ~$3.0B market cap (93.0M shares × $32.55), no debt, ≥12-month stated runway, and a late-stage lead (paltusotine, acromegaly/carcinoid syndrome) with visible commercial preparation (Europe GmbH, expanded HQ) implying regulatory milestones are approaching. The stock sits 46% below its 1-year high, so much pipeline disappointment may be priced. However, the rerating mechanism is not dated within the 90-day window — the extractions explicitly lack any PDUFA/NDA timing — and the setup carries persistent headwinds: widening losses ($298.4M FY2024 net loss, R&D $240.2M), explicit 'substantial additional financing' language alongside a live $350M ATM (dilution overhang), SBC growth ($69.4M), binary trial-readout risk, Bayh-Dole IP encumbrance on lead programs, and entrenched governance. Cheapness relative to cash plus an undated catalyst does not meet the bar for a long candidate; base rates for clinical-stage biotech outperforming SPY over any given 90-day window are modest, and the deep drawdown signals adverse momentum rather than mispricing certainty.
trades.catalyst: Paltusotine regulatory milestone (NDA filing/acceptance for acromegaly) signaled by pre-commercialization buildout; secondary optionality from atumelnant data and Radionetics/Lilly milestone events.
trades.invalidation: Confirmed dated regulatory milestone (NDA acceptance/PDUFA) for paltusotine, or stabilization above the post-drawdown range with ATM dormant — either would upgrade to long candidate; conversely, aggressive ATM usage or a negative data/regulatory surprise confirms rejection.

evidence_refs.why: $1.4B cash/investments against ~93M shares (~$3.0B cap) puts cash at roughly half of market cap with no disclosed debt — limits fundamental downside and funds launch without immediate dilution.
Late-stage lead asset in acromegaly/NETs with sizable addressable population is the core rerating lever if regulatory progress materializes.
European subsidiary and commercial buildout imply an NDA/regulatory event is plausibly near-term, but the filing discloses no specific PDUFA/NDA date — mechanism is inferred, not confirmed.
Management asserts ≥12-month runway, reducing forced-financing risk inside the forecast window.
Explicit substantial-additional-financing language plus a $350M ATM creates persistent dilution overhang that caps upside and pressures the stock in weak tape.
Interim/topline readouts can change as data matures — binary event risk cuts both ways and raises tail variance.

trades.thesis: The FY2024 10-K (Dine Brands-style franchised operator, NYQ, ~$21.69 close, -51% from 1y high) shows a deeply leveraged, structurally fragile equity story without a credible 90-day rerating mechanism. Bearish core: ~$1.2B securitized debt plus ~$0.4B lease obligations against a $216.0M stockholders' deficit; significant impairments in both 2020 and 2024; explicit disclosure that failure to refinance the 2019 Class A-2-II notes before June 2026 would trap all cash flow except a minimal management fee, and that default acceleration could transfer substantially all domestic revenue-generating assets and IP to noteholders. While covenant headroom is currently adequate (DSCR ~3.4x vs 1.20x trigger; leverage ~4.1x vs 5.25x test) and adjusted FCF improved sharply ($106.4M), these positives are already reflected in the maintained $0.51/share dividend and do not constitute a catalyst. Operations add friction rather than upside: the Nov 2024 reversal of the 100%-franchised Applebee's stance (56 units acquired, 47 retained) reintroduces lower-margin company-restaurant exposure, development pipelines are modest relative to the 3,555-unit base, and management itself cautions commitments may not convert to openings. Cheapness after a 51% drawdown is insufficient under the mandate: there is no dated near-term event (only the May 14, 2025 annual meeting) capable of forcing a rerating, while the June 2026 refinancing wall looms as a persistent discount factor. Base-rate skepticism on leveraged, drawdown-deep restaurant equities with deficit balance sheets argues against initiating.
trades.catalyst: None dated within the 90-day window beyond the May 14, 2025 annual meeting; Q1 2025 results (not evidenced here) are the only plausible rerating event, and there is no disclosed guidance or comp-sales inflection to anchor it.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would be wrong if disclosed Q1 2025 comparable-restaurant sales inflect positive and management provides credible refinancing plans for the 2019 Class A-2-II notes ahead of June 2026 — either could drive a sharp short-covering rerating given the depressed valuation.

evidence_refs.why: Failure to refinance securitized debt by term end traps essentially all cash flow except a minimal management fee — structural downside that caps any long thesis.
2019 Class A-2-II notes must be repaid/refinanced before June 2026, creating an approaching refinancing overhang that markets typically discount well in advance.
$216.0M stockholders' deficit with company-flagged risk of impaired financing ability; combined with 2020/2024 impairment history signals eroding asset coverage.
DSCR ~3.4x vs 1.20x trigger and leverage ~4.1x vs 5.25x threshold show current covenant headroom — mitigates near-term default tail but does not create upside.
$0.51/share quarterly dividend declared Feb 20, 2025 supports total return and signals cash generation, but is already known and priced into a stock down >50% from its high.
285-unit IHOP pipeline plus Fuzzy's/Applebee's commitments offer slow unit growth, but management itself cautions commitments are unreliable indicators of openings.
Nov 2024 re-acquisition of 56 Applebee's units reverses the capital-light franchised model and adds lower-margin company-operated exposure amid casual-dining softness.

trades.thesis: KinderCare-style post-IPO child care operator trading ~54% below its 1-year high ($13.53). The Q1 FY2025 10-Q shows real fundamental improvement — OCF $98.4M vs $64.1M, cash doubled to $131.3M, net income swing to +$21.2M, interest expense nearly halved, revolver undrawn — but the profit inflection is driven by one-off-ish SG&A cuts and refinancing rather than unit economics: cost of services (+3.7%) outgrew revenue (+2.1%), subsidy reliance rose to ~36% of revenue while COVID stimulus rolled off, share count grew ~30%, and $1.47B lease liabilities sit against $885M equity. Critically, disclosure controls remain NOT effective (unresolved ITGC material weakness) with an ERP implementation mid-flight through fiscal 2025 — a governance overhang that suppresses institutional sponsorship and multiples. With no hard-dated catalyst before the next quarterly report and a levered, policy-exposed model, cheapness alone does not clear the bar for a long candidate; the setup is a show-me story where the next print must demonstrate organic margin quality and remediation progress.
trades.catalyst: Q2 FY2025 earnings (early August 2025, inside the 90-day window): a second consecutive quarter of operating income expansion plus visible progress on ITGC/ERP remediation would be the most plausible rerating trigger; secondary trigger is any disclosure of deleveraging or lease renegotiation progress.
trades.invalidation: Thesis moves toward long-candidate if Q2 shows organic gross-margin/unit-economics improvement (COS growth below revenue growth), enrollment/same-center metrics disclosed as positive, and concrete ICFR remediation milestones; thesis hardens toward reject on any restatement, covenant pressure, or further deterioration in center-level margins.

evidence_refs.why: Materiality-5 bearish claim: disclosure controls not effective due to unresolved ITGC weakness, with ERP transition adding control-change risk during the forecast window — caps institutional demand and rerating potential.
Operating cash flow $98.4M vs $64.1M YoY and cash doubled to $131.3M — genuine fundamental improvement supporting solvency and modest upside optionality.
Margin gains are driven by SG&A cuts (-21%) and lower interest expense, not center-level economics; COS grew +3.7% vs revenue +2.1%, so the 'inflection' quality is questionable.
$1.47B total lease liabilities vs $885M equity and $207M due rest-of-2025 create fixed-cost downside sensitivity if enrollment softens.
~36% of revenue now government-subsidized while COVID stimulus reimbursements collapsed ($24.1M→$0.7M) — policy-dependent revenue mix raises earnings-quality and headline risk.
Undrawn $262.5M revolver (~$207M available post-LCs) plus management's 12-month liquidity assertion reduce near-term refinancing/distress tail risk.

trades.thesis: Contango-style Alaska gold producer trades ~47% below its 1-year high ($13.21) despite a step-change in fundamentals: Manh Choh's first full quarter produced $168M JV revenue, $22.3M equity income, a $24M cash distribution ($73.5M cumulative since Jul-2024), +$28.6M operating cash flow, cash of $35.2M, and a $13.8M Facility paydown. The discount is driven by optics — a $(40.5)M non-cash unrealized hedge loss, $(20.5)M stockholders' deficit, and 74,800 oz of hedges at $2,025/oz versus spot far above that — rather than by cash economics. The rerating mechanism is concrete and near-term: hedge deliveries (~12k oz/month implied by 86,739→74,800 oz during April) exhaust the book around late 2025, so each successive quarter shrinks the $98.2M derivative liability, converts paper losses back into equity income, and progressively restores full spot-gold torque while ongoing distributions (~$24M/qtr) retire the $56.1M debt stack against a small EV. Removal of the ore-haul litigation overhang (dismissed May 6, 2025) and management's no-future-cash-call statement further de-risk the story. This is cheapness WITH a credible 90-day rerating catalyst (Q2 print showing distribution #4 plus derivative mark reversal), not cheapness alone.
trades.catalyst: Q2 2025 results (~August): another large JV distribution plus mark-to-market reversal of part of the $40.5M unrealized hedge loss as deliveries continue against a ~$3,200+ spot price; progressive unwind of the 74,800 oz hedge book restores unlevered gold torque into year-end.
trades.invalidation: A missed or sharply reduced Peak Gold JV distribution, disclosure of Facility covenant stress or refinancing failure, or evidence that hedge deliveries extend materially beyond late 2025 would invalidate the thesis; also a sharp gold-price correction compressing the margin above AISC.

evidence_refs.why: AISC $1,374/oz on 57,942 oz sold confirms low-cost production; wide margin to spot underpins durable distributions.
$24M Q1 distribution ($73.5M cumulative) is hard cash flow supporting deleveraging and a low multiple of enterprise value.
74,800 oz remaining at $2,025/oz caps upside and explains the equity deficit/discount; delivery pace implies roll-off within ~6 months — the core rerating mechanism.
$24.7M due within 12 months with acceleration language; covered by $35.2M cash today but a live fragility if distributions stall.
Ore-haul litigation fully dismissed May 6, 2025 removes an overhang; residual Dot Lake suit against the Corps remains a minor tail.

trades.thesis: Deckers presents a high-quality, financially pristine profile (unqualified KPMG opinions on financials and ICFR, $1.89B cash, no debt, covenant compliance) trading ~43% below its 1-year high, with management signaling conviction via a fresh $2.25B buyback authorization (May 21, 2025) and continued open-market repurchases (~$84M through May 9 at ~$109.75). Portfolio simplification (Sanuk sold Aug 2024, Koolaburra wind-down) concentrates the story on UGG/HOKA. However, the filing supplies no credible near-term rerating mechanism: no dated catalysts, no FY2026 guidance detail, no quantified tariff exposure, and the dominant overhang — concentrated Vietnam sourcing amid live US trade-policy uncertainty plus intensifying competition explicitly targeting HOKA/UGG — remains unquantified and unresolved. Cheapness and quality alone do not satisfy the long-candidate bar; the drawdown reflects a real macro/tariff risk to a premium-multiple discretionary name, and the market can stay skeptical until the next earnings print demonstrates margin resilience.
trades.catalyst: Potential tariff de-escalation or clarity on Vietnam trade terms ahead of FY2026 order book commitments, plus the first post-guidance quarterly print (expected late July) where conservative guidance could be beaten; sustained open-market repurchases under the fresh $2.25B authorization provide ongoing price support.
trades.invalidation: Thesis weakens if tariff rates on Vietnam/Southeast Asia are implemented at punitive levels without mitigation, if the next quarterly report shows HOKA growth decelerating below low-teens or UGG wholesale weakness, or if buyback pace slows materially despite the authorization — any of which would confirm the drawdown as fundamentals-driven rather than sentiment-driven.

evidence_refs.why: Fresh $2.25B board authorization (May 21, 2025) plus active repurchases at ~$109.75 avg signals management views the post-selloff price as attractive and provides a partial valuation floor.
Unqualified KPMG opinions on financials and ICFR with no litigation or restatement flags rule out accounting-driven downside; the -43% drawdown appears sentiment/macro-driven rather than fundamental.
$1.89B cash with covenant compliance and no defaults gives balance-sheet resilience to absorb working-capital swings and tariff cost pressure without financing stress.
Predominantly Vietnam-based sourcing (<5% China) leaves gross margin directly exposed to unresolved reciprocal-tariff policy — the central unresolved bear driver with no quantified impact disclosed.

Disclosed competitive encroachment specifically targeting HOKA/UGG raises the bar for assuming growth-premium multiple recovery; excerpts contain no segment revenue/margin data to verify deceleration has stabilized.

trades.thesis: Clearwater Paper shows a genuine operating inflection — Q2 2025 Adjusted EBITDA from continuing ops of $39.9M vs $(8.6)M a year ago, sales +14% to $391.8M, gross margin swinging positive, SG&A down 14% — and the stock's -47% drawdown embeds substantial pessimism at roughly 5x annualized EBITDA on modest net debt. However, the near-term setup lacks a credible 90-day rerating mechanism: H1 operating cash flow was negative $(26.7)M (partly a one-time $57.2M tissue-sale tax payment, but also a $76.4M payables unwind), cash fell to $46.7M, the company drew its ABL for the first time ($47M), paperboard prices are still declining (-2.8% y/y), management guides flat Q3 volumes with higher Lewiston maintenance expense, and Aug 1 tariff increases threaten Canadian input costs. The R&W insurance claim (up to $105M policy limit) is a genuine potential catalyst but recovery timing/amount is uncertain and no receivable is booked. With earnings-cash divergence, unquantified PFAS exposure tied to Augusta, and springing-maturity refinancing complexity around the 2028 notes, the risk/reward is balanced-to-slightly-positive but does not meet the bar for a long candidate today. Watch for cash conversion, price stabilization, or R&W recovery news.
trades.catalyst: Potential R&W insurance recovery on the Augusta claim (policy limit $105M) within 90–180 days of the July 2025 submission would be an incremental cash/earnings event; secondarily, any stabilization in paperboard pricing or better-than-feared Q3 print despite the Lewiston outage could trigger a rerating from deeply depressed levels (-47% from 1y high).
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q3 results show continued paperboard price declines plus tariff-driven input cost inflation compressing EBITDA below ~$30M/quarter, further ABL draws beyond seasonal working capital needs, or adverse developments in the PFAS litigation; conversely, upgrade to long candidate only upon evidence of positive operating cash flow conversion and/or a quantified R&W recovery receivable.

evidence_refs.why: Q2 Adjusted EBITDA $39.9M vs $(8.6)M YoY and H1 $69.6M vs $5.6M is the core bull case: post-Augusta/divestiture portfolio is now solidly profitable, supporting a low EV/EBITDA multiple at the current depressed share price.

H1 OCF of $(26.7)M vs +$80.3M prior year (even with a one-time $57.2M tax payment) plus cash falling to $46.7M undermines earnings quality and raises reliance on revolver capacity — the key reason cheapness alone does not qualify this as a long candidate.
First-ever ABL draw ($47.0M at 5.7%) lifting total debt to $330.7M confirms internal generation is not covering capex ($80–90M FY guide); rising net debt offsets the EBITDA inflection in EV terms.

$105M-policy R&W claim submitted July 2025 against GPK sellers is the only identified near-term dated positive catalyst, but recovery is explicitly uncertain and no receivable was recognized — insufficient as a standalone rerating mechanism.

Paperboard prices down 2.8% y/y per ton (H1 -4.7%) mean the top-line growth is volume/acquisition-driven without pricing power; continued price erosion into H2 would compress the nascent margin recovery.
PFAS environmental suit naming the company over the recently acquired Augusta mill is an unquantified tail liability that caps multiple expansion until scope is clarified.

trades.thesis: Expro Group (XPRO) presents a mixed picture at $9.00, down ~62% from its 1-year high. The fundamentals are genuinely resilient: Q2 2025 operating income rose YoY ($32.6M vs $27.7M) despite a ~10% revenue decline, H1 operating cash flow surged to $89.9M (vs $16.8M), free cash flow was ~$40.6M after capex, and the balance sheet carries net cash ($206.8M cash vs $121.1M borrowings) plus $343.1M total liquidity under a newly amended facility. Management is buying back stock ($15.0M in H1 at $9.22 avg). However, the core problem is demand: Well Management revenue fell 12% YoY, margin gains are cost-cut/severance-driven rather than growth-driven, D&A is rising, severance charges jumped 165%, and the OCF improvement is partly a reversible working-capital release. In a soft oilfield-services tape, cost discipline alone rarely drives a durable rerating. Critically, there is no credible near-term rerating mechanism disclosed: no guidance beat setup, no contract awards/backlog inflection, and the buyback pace (~$7.5M/quarter) is too small relative to a ~$1B market cap to move the stock. The stock is cheap with tolerable downside, but cheapness alone does not qualify it as a long candidate under the stated framework.
trades.catalyst: No dated near-term rerating mechanism identified within the 90-day window: the $100M buyback authorization expires Nov 24, 2025 (~$60.8M remaining) and provides only modest support; Q3 earnings in late October could confirm margin durability but is unlikely to overcome sector-wide demand headwinds absent an oil-price recovery.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would upgrade if Q3 results show sequential revenue stabilization or MENA/international backlog growth alongside sustained margins, or if oil-price recovery lifts OFS sentiment; would downgrade further if Q3 shows renewed margin compression or covenant/liquidity deterioration.

evidence_refs.why: Q2 revenue -10% YoY ($422.7M vs $469.6M), led by Well Management (-12%); the top-line contraction reflects soft activity that typically caps OFS equity rerating regardless of cost control.
Operating income rose YoY on G&A cuts and lower cost of revenue — genuine margin improvement, but flagged as potentially unsustainable since it is cost-driven rather than growth-driven.
H1 OCF of $89.9M vs $16.8M prior year supports balance-sheet resilience and downside tolerance, though partly working-capital aided.
$343.1M liquidity with a net-cash balance sheet removes solvency/covenant tail risk over the forecast horizon.
$100M program through Nov 24, 2025 (~$60.8M remaining) is the only identified dated capital-return event inside the window, but at H1 pace it is too small to be a primary rerating driver.
OCF surge partially attributable to AR release/AP drawdown that may reverse, tempering the quality of the headline cash-flow improvement.

trades.thesis: The filings show genuinely improving fundamentals — Q2 subscription revenue +23% YoY, ~77% gross margin, operating cash flow swinging to +$50.3M, and $1.2B RPO backlog — against a stock already down ~42% from its 1-year high at $66.50. trades.thesis: ACV Auctions (dei_fact ticker, NYQ, $13.62, -41% from 1y high) shows genuinely improving fundamentals in the Q2'25 10-Q filed at the cutoff: revenue +20.5% YoY to $193.7M, operating loss narrowed from $(18.6)M to $(7.2)M, Adjusted EBITDA $18.6M vs $7.1M, SG&A nearly flat against +20% revenue growth (real operating leverage), and H1 operating cash flow of $80.3M vs $47.5M. trades.thesis: Fundamentals are genuinely solid — Q3 revenue +16% YoY ($189.9M), ~96% recurring mix, operating income up ($31.2M vs $25.6M), nine-month OCF $132.9M vs $116.8M, zero debt, $133.7M cash — and the stock trades ~47% below its 1-year high, implying meaningful multiple compression. A fresh $100M buyback effective Dec 1, 2025 provides a funded, dated support mechanism inside the 90-day window, and the debt-free balance sheet makes downside relatively tolerable. However, this falls short of a high-conviction long: headline growth is flattered by M&A (pro forma growth only ~8.4%), leading indicators are soft (invoiced set-up fees down YoY, one-time revenue declining), contracts are cancellable on 30–90 days' notice with no RPO disclosure, goodwill is now ~47% of assets with Carbon6 purchase accounting still provisional, other income has collapsed, and CEO/director 10b5-1 sale plans were adopted in September. Cheapness plus a routine buyback is not a sufficient rerating mechanism; absent evidence of reacceleration, mean-reversion odds over 90 days are only modestly better than coin-flip versus SPY.
trades.catalyst: $100M repurchase authorization becomes effective Dec 1, 2025 (within the forecast window) against a nearly exhausted prior program, providing a funded, dated support mechanism roughly equal to ~3% of market cap per year; secondary potential rerating trigger is finalization of Carbon6 purchase accounting (~Feb 2026) removing PPA uncertainty.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 results (or interim channel checks) show organic/recurring growth decelerating below the ~8% pro forma pace, further declines in set-up fee invoicing/new customer adds, or if the new buyback is executed slowly while insiders continue selling under their 10b5-1 plans — signaling management does not view the post-drawdown price as attractive.

evidence_refs.why: Only concrete dated event inside the 90-day window; board authorized Oct 29, 2025, effective Dec 1, 2025 — a real but modest rerating/support mechanism.
Q3 revenue +16% YoY with ~96% recurring mix and gross margin expansion grounds fundamental quality.
Nine-month OCF $132.9M vs $116.8M supports self-funded buyback capacity and downside tolerance.
Zero debt plus $133.7M cash materially lowers insolvency/forced-dilution tail risk despite the 47% drawdown.
Pro forma growth of only +8.4% vs headline +16% reveals acquisition-flattered optics — a plausible reason the market de-rated the stock and a limit on rerating upside.
Declining invoiced set-up fees are a soft leading indicator of weaker new connection activity, undermining the acceleration narrative.
Contracts cancellable on 30–90 days' notice with no RPO disclosure means revenue visibility is low; demand shocks transmit quickly.

trades.thesis: Kenvue enters the window with a signed, board-unanimous merger agreement with Kimberly-Clark (0.14625 KMB shares + $3.50 cash per share), providing a hard valuation anchor well above the depressed pre-announcement price (~$13.71, -40% from 1y high). The dominant 90-day driver is merger-spread dynamics rather than fundamentals: the consideration package implies substantially more value than the standalone price, so convergence toward deal value less a time/regulatory spread should produce positive excess return versus SPY, with the stock component adding KMB-linked upside. Fundamentals do not independently support the long case — nine-month net sales fell ~3.8%, Q3 operating income declined YoY, Skin Health & Beauty carries a fresh impairment triggering event with only ~10% goodwill headroom, restructuring costs nearly doubled, and the September 2025 acetaminophen/autism regulatory action threatens Tylenol sales — but they matter mainly as deal-break downside, not as the thesis. Improved OCF ($1,343M, +38%) and adequate liquidity support the company through pendency. Risks are real: H2 2026 expected close means a wide spread persists through the window, antitrust review and dual shareholder votes create genuine break risk, the $1,136M termination fee/no-shop forecloses rival bids, and talc/acetaminophen litigation tails remain open. Net: a credible near-term rerating mechanism (signed deal) with tolerable-but-not-trivial downside justifies long-candidate status at moderate conviction, sized as a spread-compression position rather than a fundamental value bet.
trades.catalyst: Merger-driven rerating: KVUE reprices toward deal consideration (0.14625 KMB + $3.50) as antitrust review progresses and shareholder votes are scheduled; any regulatory milestone or vote-date announcement compresses the spread within the 90-day window.
trades.invalidation: Regulatory second request or DOJ/FTC challenge extending/breaking the deal; shareholder-vote doubt; a material decline in KMB shares shrinking the consideration package; or a major adverse talc/acetaminophen litigation or FDA development triggering a MAC — any of which would collapse KVUE back toward impaired standalone value.

evidence_refs.why: Board-unanimously-approved Merger Agreement (0.14625 K-C shares + $3.50 cash) creates a hard, dated valuation anchor far above the depressed pre-announcement price — the primary rerating mechanism.
Confirms exact consideration structure and H2 2026 expected close; stock component ties KVUE to KMB performance while cash component provides a floor.
Explicitly flagged regulatory approvals, dual shareholder votes, and closing conditions — the key source of spread and deal-break risk capping near-term convergence.

Skin Health & Beauty triggering event with only ~10% goodwill headroom evidences deteriorating standalone fundamentals, meaning deal-break downside is materially below current price — limits position sizing despite the anchor.
September 2025 acetaminophen/autism allegations and FDA label-change process are an active headline tail risk that could pressure both standalone value and deal sentiment.
Nine-month OCF up 38% to $1,343M supports solvency through deal pendency and cushions the downside scenario.

trades.thesis: CareDx (CDNA, NGM) shows a genuine, quote-grounded operating inflection: Q3 2025 revenue of $100.1M (+20.7% YoY), operating loss nearly eliminated (-$0.2M vs -$13.7M), first positive quarterly GAAP net income ($1.7M), and positive nine-month operating cash flow ($20.7M). The balance sheet is clean — $194.2M cash+securities, no debt — against a ~$759M market cap (~51.4M shares × $14.77), implying EV/Sales around 1.3-1.4x on a ~$400M annualized run-rate for a business compounding revenue at ~20%. Management returned $75.6M via buybacks in nine months (~6% share count reduction) with $24.4M still authorized, providing per-share accretion and a signal at these prices. The stock sits 43% below its 1-year high, so a credible rerating mechanism exists if profitability persists. However, this is not a table-pounder: an unremediated ICFR material weakness (disclosure controls not effective, prior corrected SBC errors) creates restatement/delayed-filing tail risk, a new $20.25M litigation settlement accrual adds one-time cash outflow and residual legal uncertainty, a $250M shelf enables dilution, and Medicare concentration (~32% of revenue) exposes reimbursement risk. Nine-month results remain a net loss (-$17.2M) and $5.9M of Q3 revenue was prior-period recognition, slightly flattering the quarter. Net: attractive risk/reward skewed modestly positive, sized as a candidate rather than a conviction position given the control-environment overhang.
trades.catalyst: Continuation of the profitability inflection into Q4/FY2025 results (sustained GAAP earnings on ~20% revenue growth), continued open-market buybacks under the remaining $24.4M authorization shrinking the float, and any disclosed progress remediating the ICFR material weakness or finalizing the accrued litigation settlement — each of which could remove an overhang and support rerating from a depressed multiple.
trades.invalidation: Thesis fails if Q4 2025 results show revenue deceleration below mid-teens growth or a return to losses; if the company discloses delayed filings, restatement, or expansion of the material weakness scope; if the litigation settlement terms prove materially worse than the accrual; or if the $250M shelf is used for dilutive equity issuance rather than continued buybacks.

trades.thesis: Hamilton Lane (HLI, ~$113, -42% from 1y high) shows genuinely strong fee fundamentals: Q2 FY26 management/advisory fees +18.6% YoY to $142.1M, incentive fees +47% YoY, fee-earning AUM +$2.0B in the quarter, and H1 operating cash flow of $247.8M vs $197.1M prior year. Balance sheet is clean ($240.8M cash vs $285.6M declining debt, $325M availability, effective controls, no material litigation). A dated catalyst sits inside the 90-day window: the Guardian strategic partnership (~$5B managed portfolio, ~$500M/yr commitments for 10 years, $250M seed capital for evergreen vehicles) is expected to close at end of Q4 CY2025 with warrant issuance. However, this was announced 11/2-11/3, before the cutoff, so much of it is likely priced into the $113 close. Skeptical offsets are material: (1) earnings quality — a large share of income growth comes from volatile investment gains (Consolidated Funds net gain $17.9M vs $2.3M; equity in investees $20.1M vs $6.4M) that management itself excludes from FRE; (2) FRE definition was changed in Q4 FY25 to exclude equity comp and add FRPR including GAAP-eliminated fees, flattering non-GAAP optics; (3) compensation grew +40% YoY, outpacing revenue and compressing operating leverage; (4) six-month incentive fees were flat, implying a weak Q1; (5) structural overhangs persist (TRA liability $239.2M, dual-class dilution ~12.5M Class B units, HoldCo dependence); (6) the -42% drawdown reflects a sector-level private-markets de-rating (exit/fundraising environment) that a single partnership will not reverse quickly. Net: solid franchise with a real but partly-priced catalyst and tolerable downside — not enough edge to underwrite a fresh long today; monitor the Guardian close and Q3 FY26 print for confirmation that fee momentum is durable and comp ratios normalize.
trades.catalyst: Guardian strategic partnership expected to close at end of Q4 CY2025 (~Dec 2025): ~$5B PE portfolio management plus ~$500M/yr commitments for 10 years including $250M seed capital for evergreen initiatives, with warrant issuance marking completion; secondary support from Dec 19 dividend record date and continued evergreen fund AUM build.
trades.invalidation: Guardian transaction fails to close or terms deteriorate by end of Q4 CY2025; Q3 FY26 results (early Feb 2026) show fee growth decelerating below ~10% or further comp-ratio expansion; renewed private-markets exit/fundraising stress driving deeper sector de-rating below the post-drawdown base.

Dated near-term catalyst inside the 90-day window (close + warrant issuance at end of Q4 CY2025), but announced pre-cutoff so likely partially priced at $113

trades.thesis: The issuer (digital media/internet, trading at $32.65, -45.6% from its 1-year high) shows genuine but low-quality stabilization: nine-month revenue +5.6% to $1,044.6M, an operating income swing to +$28.4M in Q3, solid liquidity ($503.4M cash, $348.8M revolver availability, ~$130M FCF), and continued buybacks shrinking shares ~7% YoY. However, this fails the long-candidate bar on both required dimensions. First, there is no credible near-term rerating mechanism: growth is modest (+2.9% Q3), S&M is growing faster than revenue (negative operating leverage), TDS Gift Cards dragged OCF by $(47.6)M, Cybersecurity & Martech swung to a quarterly operating loss, and the only dated catalyst (~$17M of RPO recognized by year-end) is immaterial. Second, earnings quality is poor: a second consecutive annual goodwill impairment ($17.6M after $85.3M) on $1.61B of judgment-based DCF-supported goodwill following a sustained stock decline, plus a new $17.6M credit-loss write-off that drove a Q3 net loss. The $149.1M 2026 fixed-debt maturity is covered by cash but adds a refinancing overhang. A -45% drawdown with decelerating-quality fundamentals more often reflects justified de-rating than mispricing; mean-reversion alone does not constitute a mechanism.
trades.catalyst: None dated or funded within the filing horizon: the only near-term item is ~$17M of a $77.5M performance-obligation backlog recognizing by Dec 31, 2025 — immaterial to a ~$800M market cap. No guidance event, M&A closing, or debt-refinancing milestone that would force a rerating is disclosed.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would be invalidated by evidence of accelerating organic growth or restored segment profitability (Cybersecurity & Martech returning to operating profit), a credible deleveraging/refinancing plan for the 2026 maturities, or a company-specific announcement (acquisition, strategic review, large buyback acceleration) that provides a rerating mechanism — none present in the current filings.

trades.thesis: Edgewell (EPC, ~$17.40, -53% from 1Y high) has one genuinely dated catalyst: a Board-approved (Nov 6, 2025) asset purchase agreement to sell the entire Feminine Care segment for $340.0M — proceeds equal to roughly 40% of the ~$0.83B market cap — plus a fresh $100.0M buyback authorization and dividend declared Nov 13, 2025. If the sale closes within the 90-day window, deleveraging plus resumed repurchases offer a credible rerating path off deeply depressed levels. However, fundamentals argue against a high-conviction long today: operating cash flow halved to $118.4M, capex rose to $77.0M, net revolver borrowings swung to +$106.0M, restructuring costs climbed to $53.1M, corporate expense ratio rose to 7.8% of sales, and a $51.1M goodwill impairment confirms secular erosion in the very unit being sold. The filing itself concedes the sale may not close on time or at all, and credit-downgrade risk threatens financing costs. Cheapness plus an unsigned-timing catalyst is not sufficient; this is a watchlist name pending confirmation of closing progress or stabilization in cash flow.
trades.catalyst: Board-approved sale of the Feminine Care segment for $340.0M (Nov 6, 2025 APA); if closed within the 90-day window, proceeds (~40% of market cap) fund deleveraging/buybacks and validate portfolio reshaping, driving a rerating from distressed levels.
trades.invalidation: Divestiture fails to close, is delayed beyond the window, or purchase-price adjustment materially cuts proceeds; further OCF/earnings deterioration into Q1 prints; credit rating downgrade raising funding costs; revolver covenant pressure emerging.

evidence_refs.why: Concrete, board-approved $340.0M segment sale (Nov 6, 2025) is the primary rerating mechanism; proceeds are large relative to the ~$0.8B market cap.
Fresh $100.0M authorization plus dividend declaration signals management confidence and provides a capital-return support mechanism at depressed levels.
Operating cash flow halved to $118.4M while capex rose to $77.0M — free cash flow is thin, limiting standalone downside tolerance without the divestiture closing.
$51.1M impairment confirms shrinking earning power in the divested unit; combined with rising restructuring costs and corporate expense ratio, underlying earnings quality is deteriorating.
Filing explicitly states the sale may not close on anticipated timelines or at all — the sole catalyst carries material execution risk, capping conviction.

trades.thesis: JJSF-style snack/beverage company trading ~46% below its 1-year high ($88.55) after a fundamentally justified derating: FY2025 net earnings fell 24% to $65.6M, gross profit declined despite flat sales, Retail Supermarkets operating income dropped 31%, and $20.8M of plant shutdown charges plus record cocoa costs signal genuine margin/demand deterioration rather than sentiment-driven weakness. At ~19.4M shares, trailing EPS of ~$3.4 implies a mid-20s P/E — not distressed-cheap for a business with negative earnings momentum. The bull case rests entirely on undated aspirations (supply-chain transformation cost savings, six new production lines, Dippin' Dots retail expansion) and management's assertion that input inflation is 'moderating' for FY2026 — offset by explicitly flagged tariff headwinds. The balance sheet is genuinely strong (zero debt, $105.9M cash, ~$95M FCF, $210.2M revolver capacity), which bounds downside tail risk, but buyback pace was minimal (27,715 shares in Q4) and there is no dated, credible rerating event inside the 90-day window beyond a Q1 print whose direction is more likely to confirm continued pressure than inflect. Skeptical base rate: stocks down ~46% on deteriorating fundamentals with no near-term catalyst rarely outperform SPY over 90 days; the deep drawdown alone is not a mechanism.
trades.catalyst: No dated near-term catalyst identified. Nearest potential rerate event is Q1 FY2026 earnings (~late January 2026) demonstrating moderation of cocoa/input inflation and stabilization of Retail Supermarkets volumes; secondary optionality from accelerated buybacks against the $42M remaining authorization.
trades.invalidation: Thesis would be invalidated by Q1 FY2026 results showing gross margin expansion (cocoa relief flowing through), Retail Supermarkets volume stabilization, or management initiating materially accelerated buybacks — any of which would convert this into a credible mean-reversion candidate.

evidence_refs.why: Net earnings fell to $65.6M from $86.6M (-24%) with operating income $84.3M vs $117.5M — core earnings power is contracting, undermining any value argument at ~$88.55/share.

Retail Supermarkets operating income -31% to $13.3M on volume declines despite price increases — price-driven margin defense is failing, indicating demand elasticity rather than a transient shock.
$20.8M non-cash plant shutdown charges across three facilities confirm structural restructuring; benefits are real but back-loaded and unquantified.
Zero long-term debt, $105.9M cash, $165.1M OCF vs $82.9M capex — caps downside tail risk and rules out balance-sheet distress scenarios, but does not create upside.

Completed supply chain transformation and six new production lines are the only cited rerating mechanisms, but they carry no dated milestones or quantified savings — insufficient as a 90-day catalyst.
~$11.4M one-time insurance proceeds flattered FY2025 results/cash flow — underlying run-rate earnings are weaker than headline figures suggest.
Clean governance profile (single-class stock, SOX 404(b) attestation, no material litigation) removes governance-discount overhang but adds no rerating catalyst.
